title: ta_* twins disagree on default periods: correl 30 vs ta_correl 14, beta 5 vs ta_beta 14
description:
Found during the quantwave-xnaf catalog sweep. The ta_*/non-prefixed twin pairs agree on FORMULA -- all 10 were compared numerically at equal periods and every pair matches -- but several disagree on their DEFAULT timeperiod, so calling them without an explicit period silently computes over a different window.

  .ta.correl(other)     default timeperiod=30   vs  .ta.ta_correl(other)  default 14
  .ta.beta(other)       default timeperiod=5    vs  .ta.ta_beta(other)    default 14

Verified on two correlated 200-bar random walks: at equal periods the twins are bit-identical (correl@30 0.359950911442092 both; beta@14 -0.00252935308869208 both), so this is purely the default.

TA-Lib itself uses BETA default 5 and CORREL default 30, which is what the non-prefixed slugs follow -- so it is the ta_-prefixed ones, the surface whose whole purpose is TA-Lib fidelity, that diverge from TA-Lib defaults by using a blanket 14. That is the wrong way round and suggests the ta_* signatures were generated with a uniform default rather than per-function ones.

Deliverable: audit generated ta_* defaults against TA-Lib per-function defaults and fix the generator, not just these two. Check the full ta_* set, not only the ones with twins. Low priority because the formulas are correct and an explicit timeperiod avoids it entirely, but it is silent and it undermines the one guarantee the ta_ prefix is supposed to carry.
close_reason: ta_beta now defaults to timeperiod=5 and ta_correl to 30, TA-Lib's own per-function defaults, matching their non-prefixed siblings. Audited the full ta_* set: the other seven period-taking ones (ta_atr, ta_natr, ta_linearreg x4, ta_tsf) were already at TA-Lib's 14 and ta_trange takes no period, so only these two moved. Fixed in the generator via a per-function default table that errors on an unrecorded plugin rather than emitting a blanket value; regenerating reproduces the shipped signatures exactly. quantwave.talib TABETA/TACORREL inherit the fix. Regression cover in tests/python/test_ta_prefixed_defaults.py, anchored to hand-computed Pearson and TA-Lib BETA values. Commit 5b21901.

title: Lambda-distribution HMM (ldhmm parity)
description:
Close the gap between QuantWave's fixed-parameter Gaussian bull/bear HMM and the ldhmm R package / Lihn SSRN papers.

**Current state:** quantwave-core/src/regimes/hmm.rs provides online 2-state Viterbi with hardcoded bull_bear() params. No MLE, no forward-backward, no lambda emissions, no multi-state fitting, no vol forecasting, no gold-standard parity tests.

**Target:** Research-grade HMM in quantwave-core with Next<T> streaming + Polars batch parity, IndicatorMetadata, and gold-standard vectors validated against ldhmm (Gaussian mode λ=1, then full lambda).

**Primary sources (in repo):**
- references/ldhmm/ssrn-2979516.pdf — lambda HMM for financial time series, SPX 2–10 states, vol forecasting
- references/ldhmm/ssrn-3435667.pdf — composite recession HMM (out of scope for this epic; future)
- references/ldhmm/ldhmm-cran-reference.pdf — API reference (mle, log_forward, viterbi, forecast_*)
- Hamilton (1989); Zucchini, MacDonald, Langrock (2016)

**Slices:** 3 child tasks (Gaussian+EM → lambda emissions → forecasting/diagnostics). Composite macro HMM deferred.
acceptance_criteria: All 3 slices closed; quantwave_verify.sh passes; regime guide updated; existing hmm_bull_bear() preset preserved as fast default; new fit API documented.
close_reason: All 3 ldhmm parity slices complete

title: HMM slice 1: Gaussian HMM + EM/MLE fitting
description:
Extend quantwave-core HMM from fixed bull_bear() preset to a fittable Gaussian HMM aligned with ldhmm at λ=1 (normal emissions).

**Implement in quantwave-core/src/regimes/:**
- Configurable m states, transition matrix Γ, initial/stationary δ, per-state (μ, σ)
- Log forward-backward (α_t, β_t) per Zucchini §5.4 / ldhmm.log_forward
- MLLK and MLE (Baum-Welch EM or nlm-style optimizer)
- Local decoding state probs Q_i(t; x^T) — true filtering, not Viterbi-delta proxy
- Global Viterbi with backtracking (ldhmm.viterbi)
- AIC/BIC on fitted models
- Next<f64> streaming decode path + batch fit path with parity proptest
- Preserve HMM::bull_bear() as zero-config default (unchanged backtest behavior)

**Polars/Python:** .ta().hmm_fit() or equivalent; IndicatorMetadata (quantwave-i9dn)

**Gold standard:** quantwave-core/tests/gold_standard/ldhmm_gaussian_*.json — SPX or synthetic log-returns vs R ldhmm (λ=1, m=2..3). Tolerance documented.

**Source:** references/ldhmm/ldhmm-cran-reference.pdf (mle, mllk, log_forward, viterbi); Hamilton (1989).
acceptance_criteria: EM/MLE fits 2–3 state Gaussian HMM on reference series; forward-backward probs match ldhmm within tolerance; batch==streaming parity proptest; hmm_bull_bear() unchanged; nextest green; metadata exported.
close_reason: Gaussian HMM slice 1 complete

title: HMM slice 2: Lambda (exponential power) emissions
description:
Add symmetric lambda distribution emissions (ecld) to the fitted HMM from slice 1 — the core ldhmm differentiator for leptokurtic daily returns.

**Implement:**
- ecld PDF/CDF (λ, σ, μ) — exponential power / generalized normal; λ=1 → Gaussian
- Per-state λ in EM/MLE parameter space (ldhmm param matrix: mu, sigma, lambda)
- ldhmm.n2w / w2n style natural-parameter mapping for optimizer stability
- Extend gold-standard to λ≠1 cases (m=2 on SPX daily log-returns per SSRN 2979516)

**API:** emission family selector on fit config (Gaussian | Lambda); Polars exposes per-state λ and fitted params struct.

**Source:** references/ldhmm/ssrn-2979516.pdf §2; ldhmm ecld.* functions.
acceptance_criteria: 2-state lambda HMM fits SPX sample; state probs and Viterbi path match ldhmm within tolerance; λ>1 improves MLLK vs Gaussian on reference series; IndicatorMetadata updated; docs cite SSRN 2979516.
close_reason: Lambda ecld emissions, gold standard, Polars/Python DX

title: HMM slice 3: Forecasting, vol extraction, and diagnostics
description:
Research APIs from ldhmm / SSRN 2979516 on top of fitted lambda HMM (slices 1–2).

**Implement:**
- forecast_state(h) — state probability h steps ahead (ldhmm.forecast_state)
- forecast_volatility — expected vol from state mixture (2979516 § vol vs VIX/realized)
- forecast_prob — observation forecast distribution (ldhmm.forecast_prob)
- pseudo_residuals — model diagnostics (ldhmm.pseudo_residuals)
- decode_stats_history — per-bar mean/vol/kurtosis weighted by state probs
- calc_stats_from_obs — per-state summary stats from local/global decode
- Polars: .ta().hmm_forecast_*(), .ta().hmm_decode_stats()
- Optional notebook: SPX vol forecast vs sample data (no FRED dependency in CI)

**Out of scope:** composite recession HMM (SSRN 3435667 / jubilee) — separate future epic.

**Source:** references/ldhmm/ssrn-2979516.pdf; ldhmm forecast_*, pseudo_residuals, decode_stats_history.
acceptance_criteria: forecast_state and forecast_volatility match ldhmm on gold-standard fixture; pseudo_residuals exported; regime guide section for ldhmm-style workflow; nextest + pytest smoke green.
close_reason: Forecast/diagnostics APIs, gold tests, Polars/Python DX

title: Optimize Streaming Core Performance: Bitmasked Ring Buffers and Eager Batching
description:
Implement two major architectural optimizations to reduce overhead and improve SIMD vectorization in `quantwave-core` and `quantwave-polars`:

1. **Fixed-Size Ring Buffers with Bitmasking**: Replace `VecDeque` allocations with statically sized arrays (padded to a power of 2) for state lookbacks. Use bitwise AND `(idx & (N - 1))` for fast index wrapping instead of modulo arithmetic.
2. **Eager Mini-Batch Processing (`.next_batch`):** Implement a `.next_batch(&[f64])` method in the core streaming traits. This will allow the engine to process arrays in tight, auto-vectorizable `for` loops, drastically speeding up batch and Polars integrations by bypassing per-row UDF overhead.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- **Testing is MANDATORY:** Existing parity tests against `talib-rs` must pass with 100% bit-level matching after optimizations are applied.
- **Benchmarking:** Rerun both core streaming and Polars benchmarks.
- **Documentation:** Append the newly recorded benchmark numbers directly to the existing artifact at `/Users/mayanklavania/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/c97398eb-b593-47ac-bfb5-f9e435c8aa4a/performance_comparison.md`.
close_reason: Completed implementation of RingBuffer and next_batch for quantwave core, verified performance gains and passed all parity tests

title: BBANDS non-SMA matype recomputes over full history every bar (O(n) per bar)
description:
Split from quantwave-wxii as an independent performance fix worth doing regardless of the dependency work.

quantwave-core/src/indicators/incremental/bbands.rs: BBANDS::next() branches on matype. The SMA path (next_sma) is genuine O(1) incremental. Every other matype falls through to next_fallback(), which pushes the input onto self.history and then calls a batch bbands over the ENTIRE accumulated history, discarding all but the last value.

So a struct whose whole purpose is O(1) streaming degrades to O(n) per bar — O(n^2) over a series — the moment you pass anything other than MaType::Sma. On a long series that is a serious latency cliff in exactly the live/streaming path the Next<T> design exists to serve, and it is invisible from the API.

The unbounded self.history growth is also a memory leak in a long-running streaming process: it never truncates, even though only `timeperiod` values are needed.

Fix: implement the non-SMA paths incrementally. The moving-average part can delegate to the existing swappable smoothing machinery (SmoothingAlgorithm / ma_stream), and the standard-deviation part needs a rolling window of `timeperiod` values rather than the full history — note quantwave-qkft separately tracks using Welford/two-pass for stddev precision, so coordinate the two.

Ensure batch<->streaming parity proptests cover non-SMA matype values; the current test at bbands.rs only exercises MaType::Sma, which is why the fallback path went unnoticed.
close_reason: Fixed and shipped. BBANDS non-SMA matype is now genuinely incremental: the MA leg goes through the repaired MaStream and the stddev leg uses a rolling window of timeperiod values. The unbounded history Vec is deleted, so the O(n)-per-bar (O(n^2) per series) degradation and the memory leak in long-running streaming are both gone. Verified on main 3b667bfdd: bbands(matype=wma).middle equals ta.wma exactly (97.382205). Parity proptests now cover every matype, which is what would have caught this originally. Related: quantwave-qkft still tracks Welford/two-pass for stddev precision.

title: features.extract() emits Struct columns in feature_names, so to_numpy() yields dtype=object and sklearn cannot fit
description:
tests/python/test_feature_extract.py::test_integration_smoke_sklearn_fit has been FAILING on main. It is not a broken test -- it is correctly reporting a real defect, and its confusing error message is why it was mistaken for test breakage.

extract(df, feature_sets=FEATURE_SETS) returns 192 feature_names. Five of them are not numeric:

  geometric_patterns_flag        Struct({id, is_bull, pole_length, pole_length_atr, breakout_confirmed, breakout_price})
  geometric_patterns_hs          Struct({id, is_bearish, height, height_atr, score, breakout_confirmed})
  market_structure_has_flip      Boolean
  market_structure_flip_bearish  Boolean
  ttm_squeeze_is_squeezed        Boolean

Because two Struct columns are in the selection, df.select(feature_names).to_numpy() produces a numpy array of dtype=object with shape (301, 192). Any elementwise op on it raises, e.g. x != x gives ValueError: truth value of an array with more than one element is ambiguous. The test dies on that line, before it ever reaches LinearRegression().fit(x, y) -- which would also fail on an object array.

So the contract is broken: feature_names is advertised as the column list for a model-ready feature matrix, but selecting exactly those columns cannot be converted to a numeric matrix.

Deliverable: decide what feature_names means and make it true. Options: (a) exclude non-numeric columns from feature_names and expose structs separately; (b) flatten the Structs into numeric sub-columns (pole_length, height, score are genuinely useful features; id and the booleans are not); (c) cast Booleans to Float64 and drop or unnest the Structs. Booleans alone are tolerable if cast; the Structs are not usable as features under any option.

Also fix the assertion in the test to give a readable failure -- assert on the dtype being numeric before attempting the NaN check, so the next person sees the actual problem rather than a numpy truthiness error.
notes:
PARTIALLY FIXED. Struct columns (geometric_patterns_flag, geometric_patterns_hs) are now excluded from feature_names and reported in metadata['excluded_features']; they remain in features_df so callers can unnest them. The matrix is now dtype=float64 instead of dtype=object.

That uncovered a SECOND cause that the struct bug was masking -- the NaN assertion could never run before, because the object-dtype comparison raised first.

market_structure_flip_price is NaN in 294 of 301 rows AFTER the warmup trim, including the final row. That is not a warmup artefact: it is an event/sparse column that only carries a price on the ~7 bars where a structure flip actually occurred. So feature_names still does not deliver a matrix you can fit a model on without imputation, for a different reason.

Open decision, needs a human call:
  (a) exclude event-sparse columns from feature_names too, on the same reasoning as the Structs -- not a dense model feature;
  (b) forward-fill it, if 'price at last flip' is the intended semantics (check whether the NaN is meant to be carried forward);
  (c) leave it and document that callers must impute, since NaN-heavy features are legitimately usable with an imputer.

test_integration_smoke_sklearn_fit remains red pending that decision. It was already red before this fix, so this is not a regression -- it now fails with a message naming the offending column instead of an opaque numpy truthiness error.
close_reason: Fixed both causes. Struct columns (geometric_patterns_flag, geometric_patterns_hs) and the event-sparse market_structure_flip_price are now held back from feature_names and reported in metadata['excluded_features'] with a stated reason; all three remain in features_df so callers can unnest or impute them. df.select(feature_names).to_numpy() is now a dense float64 matrix with no NaN after the warmup trim, and the sklearn smoke test passes. Event-sparse membership is a declared list keyed on the indicator, not a NaN-fraction threshold on the sample, so feature_names cannot change width between training and serving. 476 python tests pass.

title: Indicator warmup is NaN not null, so drop_nulls() is a silent no-op
description:
New finding, not previously tracked. Verified against 0.7.0: a 30-row frame with rsi(14) has null_count 0 and 14 NaN values. drop_nulls() returns all 30 rows unchanged; drop_nans() returns 16. The pandas/Polars reflex for cleaning warmup (.drop_nulls(), .dropna()) is therefore a complete no-op here, and warmup rows flow straight into backtests, feature matrices, and aggregations without any error.

Compounding it: comparison signals degrade quietly rather than loudly. NaN < 30 evaluates to false, so (rsi < 30).cast(pl.Float64) yields 0.0 across the entire warmup window -- indistinguishable from a genuine no-signal period. There is no point at which the user is told the first N bars are not real.

Deliverables (decision needed): (a) emit nulls instead of NaN for warmup so Polars null-handling works as users expect -- most correct, breaking, and needs a parity sweep across all 221 indicators; (b) ship a qw.trim_warmup(df, specs) helper that slices by max warmup across the named indicators, preserving alignment; (c) make .bt reject or warn on frames whose leading rows are NaN in the signal-producing columns. (b) and (c) are additive and can land first. Regardless, document NaN-vs-null prominently -- this is the highest-surprise convention in the library.
close_reason: Shipped options (b)+(c): qw.trim_warmup(frame, *specs, extra=, strict=) slices by MAX warmup across specs so differently-warmed columns stay row-aligned (drop_nans trims per column set, which drop_nulls does not do at all); plus WarmupWarning from backtest/backtest_with_report/backtest_metrics/portfolio_backtest/walk_forward/monte_carlo/order_backtest when the signal or close column has leading NaN. Detector is try/except-wrapped so it can never break a working backtest. Docs updated: getting-started/python.md, backtest/quickstart.md, faq.md, changelog. Pure Python, no maturin rebuild. Verified independently: max-warmup slicing correct (20 not 14), zero NaN after trim, ValueError on unknown slug, warning fires on dirty / silent on clean, 425 passed + 3 pre-existing skips, doc links OK. Option (a) — emitting null instead of NaN — split to quantwave-syjj with the full architectural analysis; it is not a mechanical sweep. Branch fix/quantwave-4rsq-warmup-nan, not merged.

title: size_multiplier_col rejects Int64; coerce or error earlier with a clearer message
description: Dogfood finding 9. size_multiplier_col requires Float64 and rejects an Int64 column. Either coerce Int64 to Float64 internally, or raise a clearer up-front error naming the column and required dtype instead of a lower-level failure.
notes: VERIFIED STILL REAL 2026-08-11, AND BROADER THAN FILED. quantwave-backtest/src/lib.rs:1422 extract_f64_column accepts only col.f64() and otherwise returns InvalidDtype. size_multiplier_col reaches it via load_size_multipliers at :1219, so Int64 is rejected -- but the SAME helper is used for every other numeric column the engine loads, so the Int64 rejection is general, not specific to size_multiplier_col. Fix: try col.f64(), then fall back to col.cast(&DataType::Float64) before erroring. A few lines plus a test per affected column. Worth doing as one change rather than patching only the size_multiplier path.

title: Restore Rust quality gate in GitHub Actions (currently zero cargo build/test/clippy on PRs)
description:
PROBLEM
.github/workflows/ci.yml's `sanity` job (every push/PR to main) runs ONLY four Python
doc/metadata scripts (check_metadata_drift.py, check_doc_drift.py, check_public_metadata.py,
check_aeo.py). The `plugins` job builds/tests only quantwave-plugins via maturin, and only when
quantwave-plugins/** paths change. Result: a PR touching quantwave-core (44.6K LOC) or
quantwave-backtest (8.5K LOC) triggers NO Rust compilation or test in GitHub Actions at all.
The real gate (cargo nextest, clippy, wheel build, pytest) lives in scripts/quantwave_verify.sh,
invoked only via an opt-in local pre-push hook (scripts/install-git-hooks.sh) that is bypassable
(SKIP_PRE_PUSH_VERIFY=1) and absent on forks/fresh clones. This was deliberate — commit
8a5a2d35a "ci: move full quality gate to local pre-push hook" — rationale was CI speed.
Also missing: cargo-audit/cargo-deny (no supply-chain scanning at all), MSRV pin (no
rust-version field anywhere, no rust-toolchain.toml, edition = 2024), benchmark regression
tracking (criterion benches exist but never run in CI).

PROGRESS (2026-07-08): nextest gate landed in ci.yml (core/polars/backtest, path-filtered). Clippy -D warnings blocked (~453 existing warnings in quantwave-core tests); fmt --check blocked repo-wide drift. Follow-up: clean clippy + add fmt/audit/MSRV per original design.
design:
1. Add `rust-gate` job to ci.yml: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets
   -D warnings; cargo nextest run --workspace. Use Swatinem/rust-cache. Path-filter smartly:
   full workspace run when core/polars/backtest/plugins change; skip on docs-only changes.
   Target <10 min with cache.
2. Add `audit` job: cargo-audit (or cargo-deny check advisories) on Cargo.lock changes + weekly
   schedule.
3. Determine actual MSRV (cargo msrv find, or test stable minus 2) and pin it:
   workspace.package.rust-version, plus a CI matrix leg building on the MSRV toolchain.
4. Keep the pre-push hook as the fast local layer; document the two-layer setup in
   .github/workflows/README.md (which currently documents the no-CI-gate decision — update it).
5. Enable branch protection on main requiring rust-gate (needs repo settings — note for owner).
acceptance_criteria:
VERIFICATION (this issue IS test infrastructure — verify by exercising it):
1. Draft PR with an intentional compile error in quantwave-core → rust-gate MUST fail.
2. Draft PR with an intentional clippy warning → MUST fail.
3. Revert both → gate green; measure wall time (<10 min cached).
4. cargo-audit job runs and reports (allowlist any known acceptable advisories explicitly).
ACCEPTANCE
- PRs cannot merge to main without compile+clippy+test passing.
- MSRV recorded in Cargo.toml and exercised in CI.
- workflows README updated to describe the restored gate.
close_reason: rust-gate fmt+clippy -D warnings+nextest in CI and verify; clippy fixes across core crates

title: Unify FFI on PyO3 (abi3) — retire uniffi and the wheel-merging script
description:
PROBLEM
Two parallel binding stacks: quantwave-python uses uniffi 0.31 (build-time bindgen, cdylib);
quantwave-plugins + quantwave-backtest-py use pyo3 0.23 + pyo3-polars 0.20 (extension modules).
scripts/build_unified_wheel.py merges the outputs — this custom merge is the direct cause of the
UGLY-epic wheel-tag bug. Additionally quantwave-backtest-py/Cargo.toml points its [lib] path at
../quantwave-python/src/backtest.rs (crate source living inside a sibling crate's tree). Net:
double the interop surface, two packaging paths, confusing ownership.
SEQUENCING: the UGLY wheel-tag hotfix ships FIRST as a patch; this refactor is the durable fix.
design:
1. Migrate the uniffi-exposed API (streaming indicator classes, indicators(), doctor CLI glue)
   into a single PyO3 extension crate (merge into quantwave-plugins or a new quantwave-py crate)
   built with abi3-py39.
2. Move backtest.rs into the crate that owns it; delete the cross-crate [lib] path.
3. Delete scripts/build_unified_wheel.py — single maturin build produces the wheel.
4. Consolidate the three pyproject.toml files into one published-package config; simplify
   release.yml accordingly.
5. Coordinate with B3 (registry codegen) — the codegen targets the unified module.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD — the migration contract is the existing test surface:
1. The ENTIRE Python test suite (including B2's numerical parity suite — land B2 first) must
   pass unchanged against the unified wheel. No test edits except import-path mechanics.
2. Wheel-content test: exactly one platform-appropriate extension module per package; tag ==
   cp39-abi3-<platform>; verify_wheel_tags.py (from UGLY epic) green.
3. Install matrix 3.9–3.13 smoke (same as UGLY wheel-fix matrix).
ACCEPTANCE
- One FFI stack, one build path, build_unified_wheel.py deleted, release.yml simplified,
  B2 suite green on 3.9–3.13.
notes: PR #7 opened (feat/5ipk10-pyo3-abi3). Ported uniffi->PyO3 abi3: 50 records, 35 objects, 1 enum, 90 exports, 11 macros -> explicit #[pymodule]. 2 heck-recased names pinned via #[pyclass(name=)]; bull_bear/from_params -> #[staticmethod]. backtest.rs moved into quantwave-backtest-py. Wheel now single cp39-abi3 (bug killed at source); merge script simplified to abi3 bundler. Validated: gold 28/28, options+doctests 53/53, unified-wheel pypi_smoke pass, 15 sanity checks green. 4 pre-existing test failures (frac_diff DX + talib) confirmed identical on main -> separate bead. Awaiting review/merge.
close_reason: Merged in PR #7 (squash). uniffi->PyO3 abi3 unification: 50 records, 35 objects, 1 enum, 90 exports, 11 macros ported; wheel now single cp39-abi3 (9gek.1 tag bug killed at source); backtest.rs relocated; uniffi-bindgen removed. Incremental 'abi3-everywhere first' scope per user; single-crate collapse deferred to quantwave-6dgg. Also fixed qw.fracdiff top-level DX binding. CI fully green.

title: Python numerical validation suite — stop shipping smoke tests
description:
PROBLEM
tests/python/ = 3 files, 100 lines total. Exactly ONE test asserts numeric values
(test_parity.py::test_sma_parity — SMA only, hand-computed values). test_all_generated.py and
test_generated_plugins.py are throw-checks with print() statements; quantwave-plugins/tests/
test_indicators.py calls ~50 .ta.* methods on a 15-row frame and only checks nothing raises.
All numerical rigor lives Rust-side (4,195 lines of Rust tests, gold vectors, TA-Lib parity).
The Python binding layer — which spans TWO FFI stacks merged by a custom wheel script — has no
numeric coverage, so a marshalling bug (f32/f64 confusion, null handling, column ordering,
struct-field mapping) would ship silently to every Python user.
design:
Auto-generate a Python parity suite from the existing Rust gold-standard fixtures:
1. Pytest suite that loads each quantwave-core/tests/gold_standard/*.json fixture (27 today)
   and, for every fixture with a Python-exposed counterpart, runs BOTH the Polars `.ta`
   expression path and the streaming class path, asserting np.allclose to the gold vector
   (default rtol 1e-9, or fixture-specified tolerance).
2. The loader auto-discovers fixtures — a new gold fixture without a Python parity test becomes
   a visible skip with reason, not silence. The initial "no Python counterpart" list becomes a
   tracked follow-up list in this issue.
3. Add binding-boundary tests: warmup NaN count matches indicator metadata warmup; f32 input
   upcast policy; lazy-vs-eager equality; multi-output struct field names/order.
4. Optional cross-check layer vs TA-Lib (pytest.importorskip) for the mapped subset.
5. Wire into CI: build wheel via maturin develop (or reuse B1 artifacts) and run the suite on
   Linux + macOS.
6. CONTRIBUTING checklist: newly exposed indicator must ship with its Python parity test.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD
1. Write the fixture-loader test first; its initial run enumerates which of the 27 gold fixtures
   lack a Python-exposed API — that output is a deliverable (recorded in this issue).
2. Deliberately break one binding locally (e.g. swap two output fields) → suite MUST catch it.
   Document this mutation check in the PR.
ACCEPTANCE
- ≥25 indicators numerically asserted in Python against gold vectors (batch + streaming where
  exposed).
- Suite runs in CI on Linux + macOS; failures block merge.
- Follow-up list of unexposed fixtures recorded.
close_reason: 25 gold-vector streaming parity tests; CI matrix Linux+macOS; verify.sh wired

title: Designed Python API surface — kill reflection magic, generate explicit registry + .pyi stubs
description:
PROBLEM
quantwave/__init__.py (~lines 171-230) builds the `.ta` namespace by runtime reflection over the
compiled extension: broad `try/except: pass` swallowing import errors, string-casing heuristics
(`_cand in (_n, _n.capitalize(), _n.replace("_", ""))`), and a hardcoded list of ~20
"recently-wired" symbol names hunted by name-mangling. Consequences: (a) a Rust-side rename
silently drops a Python symbol (exception swallowed); (b) NO .pyi type stubs exist anywhere in
the repo → zero IDE autocomplete/static typing for the primary user API; (c) internal bead IDs
leak into shipped docstrings (see separate issue B9).
design:
Generate the binding surface instead of discovering it at runtime:
1. Codegen (script under scripts/, driven by metadata_export.json — 221 entries with
   names/params/outputs; later by the runtime introspection registry from the WINS-MAJOR epic):
   a. `quantwave/_registry.py` — explicit name→callable mapping; import errors raise LOUDLY at
      import time with the missing symbol named; delete the hardcoded special-name list and the
      casing heuristics.
   b. `.pyi` stubs for: top-level quantwave module, the `.ta` Expr namespace (follow the Polars
      custom-namespace stub pattern), and streaming classes — typed params with defaults from
      metadata.
2. Check generated files into the repo; CI drift check regenerates and diffs (same pattern as
   existing check_doc_drift.py).
3. Add a typecheck CI step (pyright or mypy) over an examples/typed_usage.py exercising
   `.ta.rsi(timeperiod=14)` etc.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD
1. Failing test first: set(ta-namespace symbols) == set(metadata registry names) — fails today
   (reflection gaps + pollution).
2. Typecheck step on examples/typed_usage.py — fails before stubs exist, passes after.
3. Import-hygiene test: importing quantwave must not execute any broad `except Exception: pass`
   (assert via a lint over shipped sources — grep AST for bare/broad except-pass in the package).
ACCEPTANCE
- VS Code autocomplete works for `pl.col("close").ta.<TAB>`.
- Symbol drift caught by CI; special-case list and casing heuristics deleted.
close_reason: Explicit TA_REGISTRY codegen, .pyi stubs, drift gate, reflection removed

title: De-panic quantwave-backtest production paths (FFI-reachable panics crash host Python)
description:
PROBLEM
quantwave-backtest/src has 111 .unwrap() + 6 .expect() + 2 panic!. Unlike quantwave-core (where
unwraps are test-confined), a real chunk are in production paths: walk_forward.rs lines ~88,
113, 125, 128, 212, 224, 229, 253, 256, 284, 306 (HashMap::get_mut, DataType match arms, Column
lookups); sweep.rs (22 unwraps); lib.rs (24). This crate is reached from Python via FFI — a Rust
panic aborts or poisons the host Python process instead of raising a catchable exception from
the existing _errors.py hierarchy.
design:
1. Audit every unwrap/expect/panic outside #[cfg(test)] in quantwave-backtest/src (grep-driven
   checklist in the PR description).
2. Extend BacktestError with typed variants: MissingColumn{name}, InvalidDtype{col, expected,
   got}, InternalInvariant{context}. Propagate via Result through walk_forward, sweep, lib.
3. At the pyo3 boundary, map each variant to the existing Python exception hierarchy.
4. Where an invariant genuinely cannot fail by construction, allow a documented .expect() with
   an invariant message — budget ≤10 such expects crate-wide, each with a comment stating why
   it's unreachable.
5. Enforce: deny clippy::unwrap_used + clippy::expect_used for this crate's non-test code (via
   workspace lints table or crate-level attributes with cfg(test) allows). Requires B1's clippy
   CI to be meaningful.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD — write the failing tests first, from Python:
1. Backtest call with a missing required column → expect a catchable BacktestError-derived
   exception. TODAY: panic/abort — test must currently fail (or crash), then pass.
2. Wrong dtype column → typed InvalidDtype exception with column name in message.
3. Rust unit test per new error variant construction/propagation path (walk_forward with
   malformed fold config, sweep with empty grid).
ACCEPTANCE
- Python error-path suite green; no reachable panic from the documented Python API.
- clippy unwrap_used/expect_used deny active for quantwave-backtest non-test code.
close_reason: BacktestError variants, production de-panic, deny unwrap lints, PyO3 KeyError/TypeError mapping

title: Docs long-tail quality + broken-link elimination (strict build, link check, LaTeX lint)
description:
PROBLEM
(a) Bulk-generated indicator pages have duplicated header/Description text, copy-pasted
boilerplate bullets ("Validated via proptests against gold-standard vectors where applicable"),
and filler "Typical applications". Concrete examples: docs/guides/indicators/native/dmh.md,
docs/guides/indicators/native/s_r_interaction_monitor_part_67.md — the latter is also missing
`\[ \]` LaTeX delimiters so its formula renders as raw text. docs/upgrade_to_standards.py
(1,002 lines) already names "Description duplication" and "Low word count" as lint categories —
the problem is known and only half-patched.
(b) Broken links CONFIRMED SHIPPING in the live site (checked in built site/ HTML):
site/faq/index.html has literal `href="../getting-started/index.md"` (extra `../` + .md suffix,
unrewritten by mkdocs); same class in site/comparison/index.html (`href="../benchmarks.md"`) and
site/guides/indicators/native/index.html (`href="../../DOCUMENTATION_STANDARDS.md"`). A naive
grep over docs/ finds ~150-350 more candidates with the same extra-`../` shape, heavy in the
bulk-generated "Related Indicators" cross-links.
(c) /reference/ and /backtest/ 404 on the live site (only /guides/backtest/ resolves). Redirect
stubs (rsi.md → long slug) are meta-refresh HTML instead of the mkdocs redirects plugin.
(d) No consolidated Python API reference page exists (no mkdocstrings).
design:
1. Turn on `mkdocs build --strict` in CI + add a link checker (lychee over built site/, or
   mkdocs-htmlproofer-plugin). Fix all extra-`../` links — the pattern is consistent enough for
   a mechanical scripted fix (strip one `../` level and the .md suffix where target is a nav
   page); verify each rewritten link resolves in the built site.
2. Adopt mkdocs-redirects plugin; replace all meta-refresh stub pages; add redirects (or real
   landing pages) for /reference/ and /backtest/.
3. Run docs/upgrade_to_standards.py to completion over the long tail: dedupe Description
   sections, require non-boilerplate "Typical applications" or drop the section entirely, fix
   LaTeX delimiters. Add a lint: every "Formula" section must contain `\[`/`$$` delimiters.
4. Add an mkdocstrings-python API reference page (feeds on B3's stubs/registry).
acceptance_criteria:
TDD
1. Link-check CI step MUST fail on current main (proves detection of the known broken links),
   then pass after fixes.
2. Lint asserting zero `.md`-suffixed hrefs in built site/ HTML.
3. LaTeX delimiter lint failing today on s_r_interaction_monitor_part_67.md, green after.
4. Existing duplication lint (upgrade_to_standards.py) reports zero pages above threshold.
ACCEPTANCE
- mkdocs --strict green in CI; /reference/ resolves; math renders on all indicator pages;
  meta-refresh stubs replaced by proper redirects.
notes: Broken-link elimination DONE (merged PR #5, 13dd8dbbb): fixed ~320 real broken links in 2 classes (159 .md/asset extra-../ incl. 60 candlestick market_structure; 161 directory-URL missing-../ footers) that check_doc_drift.py was masking via a wrong directory-URL resolution model + a silent skip of links escaping docs/. Corrected check_doc_drift resolution (.md/assets=file-path, dirs=directory-URL, flag escapes); added comprehensive fast scripts/check_doc_links.py to CI; added mkdocs validation: config; fixed upgrade_to_standards.py generator. mkdocs build --strict now 0 link warnings (was 362). DECISION: did NOT adopt blanket --strict as CI gate — after link fixes it still emits 13 benign warnings (griffe annotations, mkdocs_autorefs misreading docstring examples, README/index conflicts, api/ nav); the fast Python checkers (drift+links+latex) enforce links/LaTeX without that brittleness. Also LaTeX slice done earlier (PR #4). REMAINING (non-blocking follow-up): 8 mkdocs_autorefs warnings from 5ipk.6 polars.py docstring examples ([0]/[24800.0] parsed as refs); migrate 162 meta-refresh redirect stubs to mkdocs-redirects + /reference//backtest/ redirects; consolidated mkdocstrings API page.
close_reason: Substantive docs quality complete across PRs #4/#5/#6: (1) LaTeX rendering fixed + check_doc_latex.py CI lint; (2) ~320 real broken links fixed (2 classes) + corrected the masking check_doc_drift resolver + new comprehensive check_doc_links.py CI gate — mkdocs --strict now 0 link warnings (was 362); (3) description-duplication depth-lint already green; (4) /reference/ and /backtest/ 404s fixed via redirect stubs; (5) polars.py docstrings converted NumPy→Google (fixed 8 mkdocs_autorefs warnings) + fully typed options API (fixed 11 griffe warnings) → 0 polars.py build warnings. DECISION: did NOT gate CI on blanket mkdocs --strict (brittle: after fixes it still emits benign griffe/README/api-nav warnings); fast Python checkers (drift+links+latex) enforce links/LaTeX in ~1s instead. DEFERRED (cosmetic, tracked): migrating the 162 native meta-refresh redirect stubs to the mkdocs-redirects plugin — that plugin also emits meta-refresh HTML (no functional gain) and would require sync_indicator_docs.py to programmatically rewrite mkdocs.yml; the stubs work and are generator-maintained. Also pre-existing non-5ipk.5 --strict noise remains (README/index conflicts, api/ nav, bt_polars.py griffe annotation).

title: Options Polars wrappers — vectorize natively (currently Python loops) and document
description:
PROBLEM
quantwave/polars.py (~15 static methods for Greeks/IV/chain analytics) has ZERO docstrings;
parameter names unexplained (spot, strike_col, r_col_or_val, t_col_or_val); and every method
runs a Python-level list comprehension inside map_batches — i.e. per-row Python↔Rust FFI calls,
defeating the "zero-copy Rust speed" pitch precisely on the flagship Options India module. The
Rust math already exists (quantwave-core/src/indicators/options_india/, incl. the 1,118-line
iv_solver.rs — itself a candidate for splitting while in there).
design:
1. Implement native Polars expression plugins (in quantwave-polars/quantwave-plugins) for BS
   price/greeks/IV: operate on Float64Chunked slices batch-wise in Rust, reusing the existing
   options_india core math.
2. Keep the Python wrappers as thin typed façades: full docstrings (parameters, units,
   rate/day-count conventions, Examples section), preserving current signatures where possible;
   deprecation shims if changed.
3. Consider splitting iv_solver.rs (1,118 lines) into solver + term-structure modules as an
   opportunistic sub-task (do not scope-creep: only if touched anyway).
acceptance_criteria:
TDD
1. Parity FIRST: tests comparing new native expressions vs the current map_batches
   implementations on randomized chains (N=10k) — must match within 1e-10 BEFORE deleting the
   old path. Then remove the Python-loop path.
2. Gold tests: BS price/greeks vs py_vollib (or existing Rust unit fixtures) on a fixed grid;
   IV round-trip property: price(iv_solve(price)) == price within tol across
   moneyness/expiry grid.
3. Benchmark entry in the benchmark harness (UGLY/U2): record native vs old map_batches speedup
   on 1M rows (informational, not gating).
4. Docstring lint: every public method in quantwave/polars.py has a docstring with an Examples
   section (pytest --doctest-modules or a lint script).
ACCEPTANCE
- No Python-level per-row loops remain in options wrappers; parity + gold suites green; options
  docs page regenerated with the documented API.
close_reason: Vectorized all Options India chain analytics: per-strike/lookup as native Polars expressions, whole-chain reductions as single-call core FFI, zero per-row Python loops. Fixed pre-existing BS literal-broadcast bug. 26 parity tests (1e-10) + doctests wired into CI. Docs regenerated. Merged in PR #3 (3073fa947).

title: TA-Lib name mapping covers 35/221 — generate full _TALIB_MAP from parity-test ground truth
description:
PROBLEM
quantwave/talib.py maps only 35 uppercase TA-Lib names in its hardcoded _TALIB_MAP, despite the
"TA-Lib replacement" positioning and a much larger actually-parity-tested set. list_functions()
therefore under-reports coverage. The true correspondence already exists in code: the Rust
parity suites test_all_talib_parity.rs / test_missing_talib_parity.rs encode which quantwave
indicator matches which TA-Lib function.
design:
1. Add an optional talib_name field to IndicatorMetadata (Rust) for every indicator with a
   TA-Lib equivalent — harvest the initial mapping mechanically from the parity test files.
2. Codegen _TALIB_MAP from metadata (ties into B3's codegen and the WINS-MAJOR introspection
   registry); document non-TA-Lib extras (Ehlers, regimes, options) under their own groups in
   list_functions().
3. CI drift check: _TALIB_MAP regenerates identically.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD
1. Failing test first: every indicator name asserted in test_all_talib_parity.rs has an entry
   in _TALIB_MAP (write the harvest script; today count is 35 < parity-tested set → fails).
2. list_functions() group output matches metadata groups.
ACCEPTANCE
- Map coverage == full TA-Lib-parity set; drift check active in CI.
close_reason: 134-entry TA-Lib map codegen from parity harvest + CI drift

title: Restore the disabled griffiths_spectrum gold-standard test (lost fixture)
description:
PROBLEM
quantwave-core/src/indicators/griffiths_spectrum.rs has test_griffiths_spectrum_gold_standard
commented out with `// TODO: Restore test once griffiths_spectrum.json is recovered.` — the
fixture was lost and the test disabled instead of regenerated, silently reducing that
indicator's coverage to a shape-check + proptest. Sets a precedent that gold tests can vanish.
design:
1. Regenerate the fixture from the original reference: Ehlers' Griffiths predictor/spectrum
   article (check references/traderstipsreference and artifacts/*.txt parsed sources for the
   exact algorithm/source used originally).
2. If the original generation script is lost, write scripts/gen_gold_griffiths.py implementing
   the reference algorithm; validate qualitatively (spectrum peaks at known synthetic cycle
   periods) before freezing as gold.
3. Commit fixture with a provenance header in the JSON (source article, generator script, date).
4. Re-enable the test.
5. Prevention: add a CI lint failing on the pattern `// TODO: Restore test` / commented-out
   `#[test]` blocks (simple grep in the sanity job). (The systematic per-indicator coverage
   enforcement lives in the GOOD epic — this lint is the cheap tripwire.)
acceptance_criteria:
TDD
1. Re-enabled gold test passes against the regenerated fixture in cargo nextest.
2. Synthetic sanity: fixture generator reproduces spectrum peak at the injected cycle period.
3. CI lint fails on a branch containing a commented-out test marker (verify once, then keep).
ACCEPTANCE
- Test active; fixture has provenance; lint prevents recurrence.
close_reason: griffiths_spectrum.json regenerated; gold test re-enabled

title: Strip internal bead/ticket IDs from shipped code, docstrings, and docs
description:
PROBLEM
Internal tracker IDs leak into shipped artifacts: quantwave/_errors.py module docstring is
literally "Public exception hierarchy for quantwave (quantwave-1x2z)."; comments referencing
05q7, p3z9, 976r, gqem, tha, gw7s, ej8b appear in quantwave/__init__.py and elsewhere in the
published package. Internal process leaks to PyPI and reads unprofessional to evaluators.
design:
1. Sweep: grep -rE 'quantwave-[0-9a-z]{2,4}\b' over quantwave-python/python/,
   quantwave-plugins/quantwave_plugins/, docs/ — replace each with meaningful prose (the WHY the
   ticket encoded) or delete.
2. CI lint in the sanity job rejecting the pattern in shipped paths (allowlist: planning/,
   .beads/, CHANGELOG git refs, commit messages are untouched).
acceptance_criteria:
TDD: lint script MUST fail on current main, pass after the sweep.
ACCEPTANCE: zero tracker IDs inside wheel contents and the built docs site.
notes: REGRESSED then RE-FIXED (2026-07-17). Live verification found the lint green while quantwave-976r shipped in _metadata.py:10 (visible via help()). Root cause: regex required letter-led suffix, missing ~28% of base36 IDs. title: gap_momentum parity proptest tolerance too strict (flaky, FP associativity)
description:
test_gap_momentum_parity (streaming vs batch) intermittently FAILS on rare inputs due to floating-point non-associativity, not a logic error. On the shrunk seed the two paths agree to ~13 significant figures (e.g. left=17561.260625001232 vs right=17561.260625001545) — a ~1e-14 relative diff from different summation order in the streaming accumulation vs batch. The test asserts approx::assert_relative_eq!(s.0,b.0, epsilon=1e-10) at gap_momentum.rs:180; approx's default max_relative (~2.2e-16) is far too tight for accumulated sums of O(1e4) magnitude.

CI passes because its random proptest rarely hits this input pattern (mostly (10,10) closes with sparse gaps); a heavy local run surfaced it and proptest saved the seed.

FIX: relax the parity tolerance to a magnitude-appropriate value, e.g. approx::assert_relative_eq!(s.0, b.0, max_relative = 1e-9) (and likewise s.1/b.1), instead of the near-zero absolute epsilon. Then commit the regression seed file per proptest convention so the case is always re-tested.

Reproduction seed (quantwave-core/proptest-regressions/indicators/gap_momentum.txt):
cc 5a29558ad989b0af5fd10bc696a30259df3a5c204838706cf4b7c2f439bf18ae # shrinks to inputs = [(10.0, 18.55259643258196), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 17.285666525588937), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 12.968367647575961), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 19.422008668443777), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 19.35733443264069), (10.0, 18.02784274970637), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0), (10.0, 10.0)]

title: Fix wheel tag bug: py3-none wheel ships CPython-3.12-only extensions (breaks 3.9/3.10/3.11/3.13)
description:
PROBLEM
The published quantwave 0.6.0 wheel on PyPI is tagged `py3-none-<platform>` (claims universal
Python compatibility) but contains `quantwave/_backtest.cpython-312-darwin.so` and
`quantwave_plugins/quantwave_plugins.cpython-312-darwin.so` — CPython-3.12-only extension
modules (verified by downloading and inspecting the real PyPI artifact). pip will install this
wheel on Python 3.9/3.10/3.11/3.13 because the tag claims universal, and `import quantwave` /
`import quantwave_plugins` will then fail to load the compiled extensions on any interpreter
except CPython 3.12.

ROOT CAUSE
`scripts/build_unified_wheel.py::merge_wheels()` merges the uniffi-based core wheel (legitimately
py3-none for that component) with PyO3 extension wheels from quantwave-plugins and
quantwave-backtest-py WITHOUT recomputing the merged wheel tag. Neither PyO3 crate enables the
abi3 stable-ABI feature (`quantwave-plugins/Cargo.toml` and `quantwave-backtest-py/Cargo.toml`
have only `pyo3 = { version = "0.23", features = ["extension-module"] }`), and
`.github/workflows/release.yml` builds with python-version "3.12" only. Classifiers in
`quantwave-python/pyproject.toml` claim Python 3.9–3.12 support.
design:
SOLUTION (preferred): adopt PyO3 stable ABI.
1. Add `abi3-py39` to pyo3 features in quantwave-plugins/Cargo.toml and
   quantwave-backtest-py/Cargo.toml. Verify pyo3-polars 0.20 is abi3-compatible; if it is NOT,
   fall back to the matrix option below.
2. Rebuild: the .so files become `*.abi3.so`; the unified wheel tag should become
   `cp39-abi3-<platform>`.
3. Fix `scripts/build_unified_wheel.py` to compute the merged wheel tag as the MOST RESTRICTIVE
   of all input wheel tags (never inherit the first wheel's tag). This fix is required even with
   abi3, as a guard.
FALLBACK: matrix-build per Python version (3.9, 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13) in release.yml with
correct cp3X tags per build.
RELEASE: ship as 0.6.1; yank or supersede 0.6.0 on PyPI; update classifiers to match what is
actually built and tested (add 3.13 if built).
NOTE: the long-term fix (single PyO3 stack, delete the wheel merger) is a separate issue in the
BAD epic (FFI unification) — do NOT block this P0 hotfix on that refactor.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD — write these tests FIRST; they must fail against the current artifact:
1. `scripts/verify_wheel_tags.py`: opens every built wheel, parses the WHEEL Tag, lists all
   .so/.pyd members, asserts tag/content compatibility (a py3-none tag must contain zero
   cpXY-tagged extensions; an abi3-tagged wheel must contain only abi3 .so files). Run against
   the current dist/ artifact -> MUST FAIL today. Wire as a mandatory step in release.yml
   before PyPI upload.
2. CI install matrix: install the built wheel in fresh venvs on 3.9, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 and run
   `python -c "import quantwave, quantwave_plugins; quantwave.indicators()"` plus one indicator
   computation (RSI batch + streaming, results equal) and one backtest smoke call.
ACCEPTANCE
- Fresh venvs on 3.9–3.13 can pip install the new wheel and compute RSI batch+streaming with
  identical results.
- verify_wheel_tags.py passes and gates release.
- PyPI shows corrected wheels; classifiers match reality.
close_reason: abi3 wheels, verify_wheel_tags, release smoke matrix; 0.6.1 workspace bump ready for PyPI

title: Benchmarks page is fabricated — delete unmeasured numbers, build a real reproducible harness
description:
PROBLEM (live at https://lavs9.github.io/quantwave/benchmarks/)
1. Hardware section contains literal unfilled placeholders: `**CPU**: [Placeholder: e.g., Apple
   M2 Pro]`, same for RAM and OS.
2. The page claims numbers are generated by `docs/gen_benchmarks.py` "to ensure transparency" —
   but that script is 14 lines, never imports quantwave, and benchmarks `pl.rolling_mean` as an
   explicit proxy ("We'll use a simple rolling mean as a proxy for SMA if QuantWave isn't built
   yet"). It writes nothing into benchmarks.md.
3. Pandas comparison numbers are asterisked guesses, not measurements: `SuperTrend | 7.40 ms |
   >200 ms*`, `CyberCycle | 5.02 ms | >500 ms*`, `InstTrend | 73.71 ms | >2000 ms*`. Same
   numbers repeated in docs/comparison.md and the homepage/gallery ("27x/100x faster").
4. The "Streaming Latency" table is a unit-mislabeling fabrication: values 3.74/7.40/5.02 are
   the batch-throughput milliseconds relabeled as per-tick NANOSECONDS.
   `scripts/update_benchmarks_metrics.py` comments admit it: "Simple Latency simulation (as we
   can't run precision nano-benchmarks for all here easily) ... We use the previous Rust results
   as a base: 1M rows in 7.4ms for SuperTrend -> ~7.4ns per tick" — then hardcodes the table
   string.
5. The only real, reproducible measurement in the repo (`benchmark_results.md` at root) shows
   quantwave streaming SMA(14) at 6016µs vs talib-rs batch 1519µs on 1M rows — i.e. ~4x SLOWER
   (streaming-vs-batch is apples-to-oranges, but it's the only honest number and it doesn't
   support the marketing).
6. Exception: the memory-footprint numbers (41.96MB vs 88.69MB etc.) come from real
   estimated_size()/memory_usage(deep=True) measurements — this section is legitimate and can stay.
design:
PHASE 1 (same day, ship immediately): remove or neutralize every unmeasured performance number
from docs/benchmarks.md, docs/comparison.md, docs/index.md, and the gallery page. Replace with
an honest "benchmarks are being rebuilt on a reproducible harness" note. Keep the memory section.
Delete the fabricated latency table entirely.
PHASE 2: build a `benchmarks/` harness directory:
- Rust criterion benches for core indicators (SMA, EMA, RSI, SuperTrend, CyberCycle,
  InstantaneousTrendline) in both batch and streaming modes.
- Python-side comparisons (pytest-benchmark or timeit) vs pandas-ta-classic, polars-talib,
  TA-Lib, and talipp (streaming), on a deterministic synthetic 1M-row OHLCV generator (fixed
  seed, generator committed — can be shared with the datasets work).
- Harness emits machine-readable JSON including hardware info (platform/CPU/RAM via psutil) and
  exact library versions.
- The docs benchmarks page is RENDERED FROM THE JSON ONLY. No hand-written numbers allowed.
PHASE 3: CI job (manual dispatch or nightly, pinned runner class) runs the harness and commits
results JSON; the docs build fails if benchmarks.md contains perf numbers not traceable to the
JSON (extend the existing check_doc_drift.py pattern).
Publish whatever the numbers turn out to be — including honest losses (e.g. talib-rs batch SMA).
Credibility is the product here.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD — write these first:
1. Drift test: script scans docs/benchmarks.md (and comparison.md/index.md) for numeric
   performance claims (regex on ms/ns/x-faster patterns) and asserts each has provenance in the
   results JSON. MUST FAIL today (placeholders + fabricated tables present). Wire into ci.yml
   sanity job.
2. Harness self-tests: (a) deterministic data generation — same seed produces same frame hash;
   (b) correctness pre-check — before timing, all competitor libraries' outputs are compared on
   1k rows and must agree within tolerance (never benchmark wrong results).
3. Unit-label guard: the latency table is only rendered if a real per-tick benchmark ran (JSON
   key present with metadata).
ACCEPTANCE
- Zero unmeasured performance numbers anywhere in docs or README.
- Published benchmarks page shows real hardware + library versions, generated from JSON.
- Homepage/comparison claims updated to measured figures only.
close_reason: Harness + JSON throughput + render_benchmarks + claim drift guard

description:

4. Fix the "~500+" comment in docs/getting-started/python.md.
5. Refresh the PyPI long_description with the next release (0.6.1 — coordinate with the wheel
   fix U1 release).
6. Update the GitHub repo description to the canonical count.

   llms.txt source, pyproject.toml) for indicator-count literals (regex

3. Rust test: metadata export entry count equals the number of registered indicators carrying

ACCEPTANCE

- CI fails on any future drift.

title: GMM::fit() is a silent no-op — implement real EM or fail loudly
design:
PREFERRED: implement full EM, mirroring the API shape already proven in
quantwave-core/src/regimes/gaussian_hmm.rs (GaussianHmmParams/FitConfig/FitResult pattern,
thiserror error enum):
- Init: k-means++ or quantile-based initialization (deterministic given seed).
- E-step: responsibilities via log-sum-exp for numerical stability.
- M-step: weights/means/variances updates with a variance floor (avoid collapse).
- Convergence: log-likelihood delta < tol or max_iter; return
  Result<GmmFitResult, GmmError> carrying converged flag, n_iter, final log-likelihood.
- Error taxonomy matching gaussian_hmm: InvalidParams, InsufficientData{min,got},
  EmNotConverged{max_iter}.
- Signature change is a breaking change — acceptable pre-1.0; note in CHANGELOG.
IF NOT IMPLEMENTING NOW (fallback): change signature to return
Err(GmmError::NotImplemented) and REMOVE GMM from docs/homepage marketing until real.
Follow-up: add streaming/online update only if it fits the Next<T> pattern; otherwise document
batch-only.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD — write these FIRST; all must fail against the current stub:
1. Synthetic recovery: sample from 3 well-separated Gaussians (fixed seed), fit a 3-component
   GMM, assert recovered means match true means within tolerance (after sorted matching) and
   weights ≈ 1/3 each.
2. Log-likelihood monotonicity: LL is non-decreasing across EM iterations.
3. Convergence semantics: tight tol converges before max_iter on easy data; max_iter=1 reports
   converged=false.

title: Backtest engine: signal semantics and equity-based portfolio sizing
description: Umbrella for the top-priority backtest-engine gap surfaced by dogfooding quantwave 0.7.0 as the sole engine for momentum research (see trade_backtest/quantwave-dogfood.md, findings 6 and 7). Today portfolio signal is interpreted as a RAW SHARE QUANTITY, so a boolean signal buys 1 share (~0.07 percent of a 1M book) and silently returns ~0 percent, and position size cannot compound with equity. Root cause confirmed in quantwave-backtest/src/portfolio.rs allocate_entry_units: the equity/N budget is already computed but clamped by .min(cap) where cap is the signal magnitude in shares. Deliver a signal_type option plus equity-fraction sizing so equal_weight deploys and compounds capital, plus the docs to prevent the footgun. Both batch and streaming route through simulate_shared_capital, so changes here are parity-safe by construction.
notes: VERIFIED STILL REAL 2026-08-11 (main d29b96dd4). Root cause confirmed at quantwave-backtest/src/portfolio.rs:144-146: budget/price is computed correctly, then 'sign * units_from_budget.min(cap)' clamps it by cap = raw_desired.abs(), the signal magnitude in shares. A boolean signal gives cap = 1, so the position is 1 share regardless of equity. Engine fix is small and parity-safe (both paths route through simulate_shared_capital:281). The cost is blast radius, not engine work: signal_type changes what every existing signal column MEANS, touching Rust API + PyO3 + Python surface + docs + notebooks. Estimate 2-4 days, mostly plumbing and migration. OPEN DECISION: does shares stay the default (safe, footgun survives) or does weight become the default (correct, silently changes results on upgrade)?

title: Implement signal_type {shares, weight, target_pct} and equity-fraction sizing
description: Core fix for dogfood findings 6 and 7. In quantwave-backtest/src/portfolio.rs allocate_entry_units, the EqualWeight budget equity/N is already equity-based and compounds, but the realized size is min(equity/N/price, abs(signal)) so the signal magnitude acts as a hard share-count ceiling; a boolean signal clamps to 1 share. Add a signal_type enum: shares (today's behavior, keep for back-compat), weight (budget = equity times abs(signal), e.g. 0.1 = 10 percent of equity), target_pct (normalized across active names like SignalWeighted). Drop the .min(cap) share clamp for weight/target_pct modes. Thread the option through the Python .bt.portfolio_backtest surface. Preserve batch<->streaming parity (both go through simulate_shared_capital) and the lookahead-free property (equity is current mark-to-market). OPEN DECISIONS from the user: (a) default mode -- flip to weight/inclusion vs keep shares; (b) weight semantics -- fraction of total equity vs normalized across active names.

design:
# Deep Extraction + Streaming Design: MQL5 Part 66 Head & Shoulders Scanner (lynnchris)

**Task**: quantwave-bfg  
**Completed**: 2026-05-30 IST (full source obtained + analyzed)  
**Status update**: Research extraction complete; ready for implementation under cu03.

## Primary Sources (recorded verbatim)
- Article: https://www.mql5.com/en/articles/22194  
  "Price Action Analysis Toolkit Development (Part 66): Developing a Structured Head and Shoulders Scanner in MQL5" by Christian Benjamin (lynnchris), published ~23 April 2026.
- Download ZIP (confirmed working): https://www.mql5.com/en/articles/download/22194.zip
- Local persisted source (for reference + audits): `references/MQL5/lynnchris/Part66/HS_Indicator.mq5` (24,171 bytes, 598 lines, dated 04-23-2026 in archive)
- Series hub: https://www.mql5.com/en/users/lynnchris/publications (70+ parts)
- Cross-referenced in project: Parts 21 (swings/MarketStructure), 67 (S/R monitoring), 69 (Flags), 70 (signal buffer refactor lesson). All from same series.

**Key quote from code header**:
```
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
//|                                                 HS Indicator.mq5 |
//|                                  Copyright 2026, MetaQuotes Ltd. |
//|                                             https://www.mql5.com |
//+------------------------------------------------------------------+
#property link      "https://www.mql5.com/en/users/lynnchris"
```

**Key quote on intent** (from article summaries + code structure):
Addresses "difficulty of consistently identifying Head and Shoulders ... due to noise, asymmetry, and varying neckline slopes" via "structured, rule-based" scanner with scoring, filters, and breakout detection. "The structured approach significantly reduces the ambiguity typical of classical pattern recognition."

## Input Parameters (exact from source + comments)
```mql5
input int      SwingStrength       = 3;            // Swing detection strength
input double   ShoulderTolerance   = 0.02;         // Shoulder price tolerance (2%)
input double   MinPatternSizeATR   = 1.5;          // Min pattern height in ATR
input double   MaxNecklineSlopeDeg = 30.0;         // Max neckline slope (degrees) - 30° allows gentle upward/downward
input bool     AllowDescendingNeck = true;         // Allow descending necklines (rare but valid)
input int      MinTimeSymmetry     = 50;           // Min time symmetry % (0-100)
input bool     ShowNeckline        = true;
input bool     ShowBreakoutArrow   = true;
input bool     AlertOnNewPattern   = true;
input int      MinSwingDistance    = 10;
input int      MinPatternDistance  = 50;
input double   MinScoreThreshold   = 60.0;
input color    PatternFillColor    = clrYellow;
input int      PatternOpacity      = 60;
```
ATR handle is hard-coded to 14 periods inside OnInit (not an input).

**Rationale observed in code**:
- SwingStrength=3: 5-bar window (i-SwingStrength to i+SwingStrength) for local extremum.
- ShoulderTolerance=0.02 (2% of head price): allows small asymmetry while rejecting gross imbalance.
- MinPatternSizeATR=1.5: filters noise; pattern must be meaningful relative to volatility.
- MaxNecklineSlopeDeg=30 + AllowDescendingNeck: classic "flat-ish" neckline preference with opt-in for real-market tilt.
- MinTimeSymmetry=50: left/right leg bar counts must be reasonably balanced.
- MinSwingDistance / MinPatternDistance: anti-overlap and minimum formation time guards.
- Score threshold 60/100: tunable quality gate before emitting.

## Core Structures (verbatim)
```mql5
struct SwingPoint
  {
   int               barIndex;
   double            price;
   bool              isHigh;
   datetime          time;
  };

struct Pattern
  {
   int               id;
   bool              isBearish;
   int               lsIndex,headIndex,rsIndex;
   int               neck1Index,neck2Index;      // Low after LS (neck1) and low before RS (neck2)
   double            neckSlope,neckIntercept;
   double            headPrice,neckPriceAtHead,height;
   double            score;
   bool              signalGenerated;
   datetime          signalTime;
   int               signalBar;
   datetime          detectionTime;
  };
```

## Algorithm Pipeline (high-fidelity pseudocode from source)
1. **OnCalculate** (new bar guard via static lastTime):
   - DetectSwings(time, high, low, bars)  // full re-scan every bar
   - DetectPatterns(...) 
   - CheckBreakouts(time, close, 0)

2. **DetectSwings**:
   - For i in [SwingStrength .. bars-SwingStrength-1]:
     - isHighSwing if high[i] >= all high in [i-S..i+S]
     - isLowSwing symmetrically
     - Push SwingPoint {barIndex=i, price, isHigh, time} to g_swings[] (global resize)

3. **DetectPatterns** (bearish first):
   - Require >=5 swings
   - For each window of 5 consecutive swings:
     - Bearish candidate: H L H L H  (indices i, i+1, i+2, i+3, i+4)
       - Span check: rs.bar - ls.bar >= MinSwingDistance
       - Head dominance: head.price > ls.price && head.price > rs.price
       - Shoulder symmetry: |ls.price - rs.price| / head.price <= ShoulderTolerance
       - Neckline: linear between n1 (low after LS) and n2 (low before RS)
       - height = head.price - neckAtHead; reject if height < MinPatternSizeATR * atr
       - if (!AllowDescendingNeck && slope < 0) reject
       - score = ComputePatternScore(...)
       - if score >= MinScoreThreshold → candidate
     - Bullish (inverse): symmetric L H L H L logic, height = neckAtHead - head.price
   - Dedup among candidates (close heads within MinPatternDistance → keep higher score, mark loser -1)
   - Filter score >= threshold again
   - For each surviving candidate: existence check against g_patterns by (ls,head,rs) indices → if new: append, DrawPatternTriangles, DrawNeckline, alert

4. **ComputePatternScore** (exact, 0-100):
   ```mql5
   double priceDiff = Abs(leftShoulder - rightShoulder) / headPrice;
   double priceSym = Max(0, 1 - priceDiff / ShoulderTolerance);
   score += priceSym * 30.0;

   // time
   leftDist = headIndex - lsIndex; rightDist = rsIndex - headIndex;
   timeRatio = Min(left,right) / Max(left,right);
   score += timeRatio * (MinTimeSymmetry/100.0) * 20.0;

   // slope
   slopeDeg = Arctan(neckSlope)*180/PI;
   if (Abs(slopeDeg) <= MaxNecklineSlopeDeg)
       score += 20.0 * (1 - Abs(slopeDeg)/MaxNecklineSlopeDeg);

   // size
   sizeRatio = height / atr;
   sizeScore = Min(30.0, (sizeRatio / MinPatternSizeATR) * 30.0);
   score += sizeScore;
   return Min(100.0, score);
   ```

5. **CheckBreakouts** (per bar, per pattern not yet signaled):
   - neckCurrent = neckSlope * currentBar + neckIntercept
   - breakout = (bearish && close < neckCurrent) || (bullish && close > neckCurrent)
   - if yes: set signalGenerated/signalTime/signalBar, DrawBreakoutArrow, alert

6. **Drawing** (heavy, separate from signals):
   - DrawPatternTriangles: 3 filled OBJ_TRIANGLE (LS/Head/RS regions) using extra outer low/high swings for "neck0/neck3" anchors + actual ls/head/rs/neck points.
   - DrawNeckline: OBJ_TREND (dashed magenta) extended to outer swings + text label.
   - Breakout: OBJ_ARROW up/down.
   - Full ObjectsDeleteAll(g_prefix) on init/deinit.
   - Prefix "HS_"

**Critical observation (Part 70 lesson context)**: Despite rich internal state (signalGenerated etc.) and alerts, the **primary "output" the author chose is chart objects**. This is the exact anti-pattern called out in the cu03 research for Parts 69-70. For QuantWave we invert priority: rich Struct events + metadata first; optional visualization layer later.

## Edge Cases & Implementation Notes from Source
- No swing eviction: g_swings[] and g_patterns[] grow for the life of the indicator (fine for typical chart lengths).
- Strict 5-swing contiguous sequence only (no gaps, no "complex" H&S variants in this v1).
- Neckline always drawn from the two specific internal lows/highs (n1/n2), then extended for viz.
- ATR fetched fresh each DetectPatterns (single value, not series).
- Duplicate prevention is index-based (exact ls/head/rs), not fuzzy.
- Alerts only on first detection and first breakout (guarded by flags).
- No statistical validation or backtest results in the code comments (pure construction + visualization tool).

## Streaming Design Sketch for QuantWave (Next<T> + Polars parity)

**Strong recommendation**: Do **not** port the monolithic indicator. Compose on the shared SwingAnalyzer + MarketStructure state machine from cu03 child `quantwave-iuzv` (Part 21 foundation). H&S becomes a higher-order detector.

### Option A (preferred for parity & reuse) — Event-driven on swings
```rust
// In new features or indicators/price_action/
pub struct HeadAndShouldersDetector {
    // Receives swing events or polls recent swings from shared SwingAnalyzer
    recent_swings: VecDeque<SwingPoint>,   // ring buffer, capacity ~30-50
    active_patterns: Vec<HsPatternState>,  // patterns still watching for breakout
    next_id: u32,
    params: HsParams,  // SwingStrength (or delegate), ShoulderTolerance, ...
    atr_provider: Box<dyn Next<f64> + ...>, // or external ATR series
}

impl Next<Bar> for ... { ... }  // or better: Next<SwingEvent> if we make swings first-class events

// On new confirmed swing:
- push to recent_swings (evict old)
- run 5-swing window matcher on last 5-7 swings (only when a new swing arrives)
- apply all filters (head dominance, shoulder tol, height vs current ATR, slope)
- compute score
- if >= threshold and not duplicate (by swing indices or normalized key): emit HsPatternDetected event/struct, store in active_patterns with breakout watch state
- For each active: on every bar (or on price update) eval neckline at current bar index, detect breakout once, emit HsPatternBreakout, remove or mark completed
```

### Option B (simpler incremental, still correct)
Maintain the last N bars of OHLC + running ATR. On each bar:
- Incremental swing detection (maintain small deque of recent candidates, confirm when out of window — similar to existing BillWilliamsFractals but with configurable strength + ATR depth if we generalize).
- Run the geometric 5-swing matcher only on the recent swing list (much smaller than full history).
- Same state machine for active patterns + breakout watching.

**Parity guarantee**: The batch Polars version (using the same SwingAnalyzer logic + windowed pattern search over a LazyFrame of swings) must produce identical detection times + identical scores + identical breakout bars as the streaming collector.

**Rich output (for backtester + ML confluence)**:
```rust
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)]  // Polars-friendly via Struct
pub struct HsPattern {
    pub id: u32,
    pub is_bearish: bool,
    pub ls: SwingRef { bar: usize, price: f64, time: ... },
    pub head: SwingRef,
    pub rs: SwingRef,
    pub neck1: SwingRef,
    pub neck2: SwingRef,
    pub neck_slope: f64,
    pub neck_intercept: f64,
    pub height: f64,
    pub height_atr: f64,           // critical for position sizing
    pub score: f64,                // 0-100
    pub price_symmetry: f64,       // component scores for debugging / ML
    pub time_symmetry: f64,
    pub slope_quality: f64,
    pub size_quality: f64,
    pub detection_bar: usize,
    pub breakout_confirmed: bool,
    pub breakout_bar: Option<usize>,
    pub breakout_price: Option<f64>,
    // Optional: regime_at_detection, feature_vector_at_detection (injected later)
}
```
Emit as Struct series or exploded columns. Backtester can read height_atr for risk, score for conviction filters.

## Property Invariants (mandatory for proptests + synthetic validation)
1. Every emitted pattern has head strictly dominant (head.price > ls && head > rs for bearish; opposite for bullish).
2. Shoulder price diff / head <= ShoulderTolerance (within floating tolerance).
3. If !AllowDescendingNeck, emitted patterns have neck_slope >= 0 (for bearish convention).
4. |neck_slope in degrees| <= MaxNecklineSlopeDeg for all emitted (or the filter was off).
5. height >= MinPatternSizeATR * atr_at_formation.
6. time symmetry ratio >= MinTimeSymmetry/100 (when MinTimeSymmetry > 0).
7. score >= MinScoreThreshold for every emitted HsPattern (pre-breakout).
8. No two patterns share the exact same (ls, head, rs) bar indices (dedup).
9. Breakout is emitted at most once per pattern (signalGenerated guard).
10. On synthetic "perfect symmetric flat-neck H&S with height=2.0*ATR and score=92": detector must emit exactly one pattern with score in [90,95] range and correct is_bearish.
11. On pure noise (no 5-swing sequences meeting dominance): zero patterns.
12. Streaming collect() and batch Polars implementation agree on detection_bar and breakout_bar (within 0-1 bar tolerance for boundary effects) and identical scores (approx 1e-6).

## Synthetic Generator Ideas (for the PA validation harness child 5mfc)
- Generator 1 (clean): Construct exact 5-bar-index swings with controlled prices. Set ATR constant. Vary symmetry params, slope (0 to 45°), height (0.5-4.0 ATR). Label ground truth "should detect / should reject".
- Generator 2 (noisy): Take clean pattern, add Gaussian noise (sigma = 0.1-0.5 * ATR) to price and/or time jitter (±1-3 bars on shoulders). Measure recall vs noise level.
- Generator 3 (stress): Inject two overlapping candidate heads close together → assert dedup keeps the higher-score one.
- Generator 4 (regime): Combine with existing regime synthetics; assert "only emit H&S in trending regimes if we add optional filter later".
- Use proptest strategies for the numeric params (ShoulderTolerance, MaxSlope, etc.) and verify all invariants hold on generated series.
- Store generator + expected event metadata in the canonical notebook.

## Cross-References & Gaps vs Current QuantWave Code
- `quantwave-core/src/indicators/fractals.rs`: BillWilliamsFractals is the closest primitive (fixed 5-bar local high/low). Excellent parity tests + gold. This Part 66 uses identical local-extremum idea but with configurable SwingStrength and then a full 5-swing geometric sequencer + neckline + scoring on top. Improvement path: make a generalized SwingDetector (fixed or ATR-adaptive depth from Part 21) that both fractals and this can use.
- `rodc.rs`: Zigzag flip rate — useful as a "noisiness" feature to down-weight pattern confidence in high-RODC regimes.
- `pivot_points.rs` + `pattern.rs` (CDL only): No geometric chart pattern support today. This + Flags (69) fill exactly that layer.
- Existing `regimes/`: Natural post-filter / feature (e.g., only trust H&S in HMM state "trending").
- Backtester (`quantwave-backtest`): Already comments reference "rich signal metadata readiness: MQL5 PA series (Parts 69-70, 67)". This struct shape (height_atr, score, breakout_confirmed) is exactly what was anticipated for dynamic sizing.
- No current equivalent of neckline geometry or 5-swing pattern scoring.

**Gaps in original that we will improve**:
- Full-history re-scan every bar → incremental swing list + windowed matcher.
- ATR hard-coded 14 → pluggable ATR provider.
- Viz objects as primary output → rich Struct events primary (drawing as optional plugin).
- No streaming state machine concept → full Next<T> + batch parity.

## Relation to cu03 Epic & Children
- Directly satisfies the "geometric research (quantwave-bfg)" feeder for child `quantwave-ej8b` "Geometric Pattern Detectors (Flags + H&S) built on new Swing/Structure foundation".
- Strongly recommends **implementing the shared Swing + MarketStructure foundation (quantwave-iuzv / Part 21) first**; then H&S validator becomes thin and clean.
- Rich event system (bmkn) must support this + future Flags/Wedges.
- Validation harness (5mfc) must include the synthetic + invariant suite described above.
- Confluence layer (8aht) will combine HsPattern.score + regime + ML features.

## Remaining Related Research (recommended)
- Part 69 (Flags scanner) — same series, same author, similar swing + geometry + scoring philosophy. If Flags are high priority for v0.1 geometric, run an identical focused bfg-style deep extraction (download its .mq5, same structure).
- Part 70 signal buffer refactor — the explicit "lessons learned on clean outputs".
- Any confluence or wedge parts that reuse the same swing foundation.

This extraction provides a high-fidelity, source-recorded basis for a correct, parity-guaranteed, backtester-ready H&S implementation that matches the project's Universal Indicator + rich metadata + synthetic validation standards.

**No blocking unknowns remain for the core H&S logic.** Minor tunable details (exact window extension for neckline drawing anchors) can be simplified or made configurable in the QuantWave port.

| 8 | `backtest_with_report()` end-to-end | `test_backtest_with_report_returns_report` | BacktestReport { result, metrics } |

- Part 67: Real-time S/R interaction monitoring (touches, breakouts, retests) — including support for manually/user-drawn levels.
- Recurring critical lesson (Parts 69-70, 67): Separate visualization from clean, structured, machine-readable signal outputs with rich metadata (e.g. pole height, flip strength, confluence score) for automation and the backtester.

title: Indicator Bible: Rich Documentation Enhancement
description:
## Indicator Bible: Rich Documentation Enhancement

### Goal
Make the QuantWave Indicator Bible the definitive reference for all 91 indicators — richer than TradingView tooltips, better than Wikipedia, precise enough for quants.

### Three New Fields on IndicatorMetadata (metadata.rs)
Every indicator gains three new fields. The struct field order is: name → description → usage → keywords → ehlers_summary → params → formula_source → formula_latex → gold_standard_file → category.

1. **usage**: &'static str — 1-2 sentence plain-English explanation of WHEN and WHY a trader uses this. Focus on: entry signals, trend confirmation, noise filtering, position sizing, or whatever is specific to that indicator. Do NOT restate the math.

2. **keywords**: &'static [&'static str] — array of searchable lowercase tags. Examples: &["momentum", "oscillator", "overbought", "oversold"], &["trend", "adaptive", "moving-average", "dsp"]. 3-6 tags per indicator. Tags come from: [momentum, oscillator, trend, filter, cycle, adaptive, moving-average, dsp, ehlers, smoothing, breakout, volatility, support-resistance, mean-reversion, prediction, spectral, high-pass, low-pass, zero-lag, classic, pattern, statistics, pairs-trading].

3. **ehlers_summary**: &'static str — 3-4 authoritative lines. For Ehlers indicators: paraphrase or short direct quote from Cybernetic Analysis (2004), Rocket Science for Traders (2001), Cycle Analytics (2013), or the relevant paper. For classic indicators (SMA, ATR, etc.): use StockCharts ChartSchool as authority. If quote is short (<100 chars) use it verbatim with attribution. If longer, paraphrase tightly.

### Source Priority for ehlers_summary
1. Ehlers books: Cybernetic Analysis (2004), Rocket Science for Traders (2001), Cycle Analytics for Traders (2013)
2. Ehlers papers (see references/Ehlers Papers/)
3. TradingView Pine Script builtin descriptions
4. StockCharts ChartSchool (for classic indicators)

### Rendering in mdBook
- keywords render as <span class="kw-badge"> HTML chips in the generated .md files
- category renders as <span class="category-badge">
- ehlers_summary renders as a blockquote (> prefix) under ## Background
- usage renders under ## Usage section
- The xtask generator (quantwave-xtask/src/main.rs) must extract all new fields from the AST

### Scope by Subtask
- quantwave-7ox: metadata.rs struct extension (already done)
- quantwave-ead: 66 Ehlers DSP category indicators
- quantwave-[task3]: 24 Classic category indicators
- quantwave-[task4]: xtask AST parser + badge renderer update
- quantwave-[task5]: mdBook custom CSS for .kw-badge and .category-badge chips, verify build

### Compile Constraint
After ALL indicator files are updated AND metadata.rs has the new fields, run: cargo nextest run — must pass all 233+ tests with zero failures.
close_reason: All subtasks completed. Indicator Bible is now fully enriched.
