title: Epic: Backtest output contract — typed metrics, documented units, AI-agent ready
description:
# Epic: Backtest Output Contract (AI-Agent Ready)

## Problem

External AI agents integrating QuantWave 0.6.0 report the #1 friction is **undocumented dict keys and unstated units/signs** on backtest outputs (`metrics()`, `stats()`, `trades()`, `equity_curve()`). Keys mostly exist today but are untyped plain dicts; conventions (fractions vs percent, drawdown sign, epoch timestamps, fill vs raw price) are implicit.

**Scope:** Backtest engine output contract only — NOT per-indicator metric standardization.

## Empirically verified contract (0.6.0 baseline)

### `metrics()` → PerformanceMetrics (all return-like values are **fractions**, not percent)

| Key | Definition | Units / sign |
|-----|------------|--------------|
| `total_return` | final/initial − 1 | fraction |
| `cagr` | annualized return | fraction |
| `sharpe_ratio` | annualized, risk-free = 0 | ratio |
| `sortino_ratio` | annualized downside | ratio |
| `max_drawdown_pct` | peak-to-trough decline | **positive fraction** (0.10 = 10% drawdown) |
| `win_rate` | winners / closed trades | 0–1 |
| `profit_factor` | gross profit / gross loss | ratio; inf if no losses |
| `num_trades` | closed trade count | count |
| `avg_trade_pnl` | mean net PnL per trade | currency |
| `final_equity` | ending portfolio value | currency |

### `stats()` → summary dict (stable keys)

`initial_cash`, `num_trades`, `net_pnl`, `final_equity`, `total_return` (+ optional `num_symbols`, `portfolio_mode` for multi-symbol)

### `trades()` → Polars DataFrame columns

`trade_id`, `side` (+1 long / −1 short), `entry_ts`/`exit_ts` (Unix epoch **seconds**; `exit_ts` null = open at series end), `entry_price`/`exit_price`, `quantity`, `pnl_net` (net of commission).

**Gap vs agent spec:** Rust `Trade` also has `entry_fill_price`/`exit_fill_price` (slippage-adjusted) but DataFrame export currently uses raw `entry_price`/`exit_price`. Epic must either export fill columns or document actual behavior.

### `equity_curve()` → columns

`ts` (epoch sec), `equity`, `cash`, `position` (signed units), `close` (+ optional `symbol`)

### `BacktestConfig` conventions (one-line each)

- `stop_loss_pct` / `take_profit_pct` / `trailing_stop_pct`: **fractions** (0.05 = 5%)
- Default position size: **1 unit** unless `size_multiplier_col` set
- `execution_delay="same_bar"`: fill on signal bar

## Approach (TDD-first)

1. **Lock behavior with tests** against Rust source + existing `quantwave-backtest/tests/gold_standard/metrics_basic.json` — do NOT test every indicator.
2. Add Python contract tests (`test_backtest_output_contract.py`) asserting keys, types, units, sign of `max_drawdown_pct`.
3. Introduce typed Python surfaces (`PerformanceMetrics`, `BacktestStats` TypedDict or `@dataclass`) returned by `metrics()`/`stats()` with field docstrings.
4. Document in mkdocstrings + `docs/guides/backtest/output-contract.md` for LLM citation.
5. Optional: expose `PerformanceMetrics` as PyO3 pyclass (keep dict compat via `.as_dict()`).

## Out of scope

- Per-indicator output standardization
- Changing metric formulas without gold-standard update + source citation
- Breaking rename of existing dict keys in 0.6.x (additive typing only)

## Success metrics

- AI agent can call `.metrics()` without hand-decoding units
- `max_drawdown_pct` sign documented and tested
- `quantwave_verify.sh` includes output contract tests
close_reason: All slices implemented, tests passing, schema stable

title: Doc depth quality lint — detect thin long-tail native pages
description:
## Expectation

Extend docs/upgrade_to_standards.py (or add scripts/check_doc_depth.py) with a **depth lint** beyond structural --lint. Structural lint only checks headings exist; depth lint catches template-quality pages that fail DOCUMENTATION_STANDARDS.md intent.

## Depth rules to enforce (automated)

Flag a page FAIL if ANY of:

1. **Description duplication** — first paragraph of ## Description equals metadata.description verbatim (no enrichment beyond one repeat).
2. **Generic edge bullets** — Edge Cases contains the exact bulk-upgrade boilerplate string "QuantWave implements this indicator via the universal Next<T> trait" OR fewer than 4 distinct edge bullets.
3. **Broken Polars example** — Usage Examples Polars block contains `.ta.<method>("close",` (wrong signature pattern) OR uses `map_batches` loop when a `.ta.<method>()` exists in quantwave-polars.
4. **Missing warmup specificity** — Edge Cases does not mention a numeric warmup bar count when metadata has a known period default (scalar indicators).
5. **Low word count** — Description section (between ## Description and ## Formula) under 80 words for non-pattern indicators; under 50 for patterns.

## Deliverables

- `python docs/upgrade_to_standards.py --depth-lint` OR `python scripts/check_doc_depth.py`
- Report: list failing slugs + violation reason (JSON or stdout table)
- Document depth bar in docs/DOCUMENTATION_STANDARDS.md § Enforcement (append Phase 3 depth rules — one short subsection)
- Baseline report committed as planning/doc_depth_baseline.json (optional) so enrichment task can track progress

## Impact when done

CI/agents can objectively list which pages need hand enrichment vs which are exemplar-quality. Stops claiming "100% STANDARDS" when only structure passes.

## Do NOT

- Bulk-rewrite all pages in this task (that's the enrichment child)
- Change indicator math or metadata

1. Depth lint script exists and runs from repo root.
2. `python docs/upgrade_to_standards.py --depth-lint` exits 0 only when zero violations (or exits 1 with slug list — document expected baseline count in PR).

title: Metadata-driven native page generator (export_metadata JSON)
description:
## Expectation

Replace the legacy quantwave-xtask syn generator (emits ## Usage / ## Background / ## Formula) with a **single source of truth** pipeline:

```
cargo run -p quantwave-core --bin export_metadata  →  JSON
        ↓
doc generator (Rust xtask and/or Python)  →  docs/guides/indicators/native/<slug>.md
```

Generated pages MUST match DOCUMENTATION_STANDARDS.md mandatory headings (same output as upgrade_to_standards.py render_page()).

## Implementation options (pick one, document in PR)

**Option A (recommended):** Python `scripts/generate_native_docs.py` reads export_metadata JSON + parses polars API from lib.rs — reuses upgrade_to_standards.py render functions.

**Option B:** Refactor quantwave-xtask to call export_metadata binary and port render logic to Rust.

Either way, `cargo xtask docs` or `python scripts/generate_native_docs.py` becomes the canonical regen command in contributing.md.

## Registry ↔ filesystem reconciliation

- 216 registered slugs vs 227 md files today — generator must:
  - Emit page for every ALL_REGISTERED slug
  - Report orphan md files (no registry entry)
  - Respect SKIP_FILES (PA guides) — never overwrite

title: calmar_ratio still returns inf for zero drawdown; align with the NaN-for-undefined convention
description:
Follow-up spotted while fixing quantwave-s3iu. That issue changed sortino_ratio and profit_factor to return NaN rather than inf when their denominator is empty, on the reasoning that inf reads as a value while NaN reads as undefined. calmar_ratio = cagr / max_drawdown_pct was left alone because it is an extended metric and was outside that scope, so it still returns inf when max_drawdown_pct is zero and CAGR is positive. Verified post-fix: extended_metrics()["calmar_ratio"] is inf on a single-trade run whose sortino_ratio and profit_factor are both now NaN — the same bundle now uses two different conventions for the same condition, which is worse than either convention applied consistently.

Deliverable: return NaN for calmar_ratio when max_drawdown_pct is zero, and update the units/sign column in docs/guides/backtest/output-contract.md, which currently documents inf as the expected value. Check the same sweep for any other ratio in extended_metrics with a potentially-empty denominator. Note the walk-forward selection interaction found in s3iu: a v > best_val comparison lets inf win, so an optimizer can select a degenerate zero-drawdown variant; NaN never compares greater and is skipped. calmar_ratio is a plausible walk-forward objective, so this is not purely cosmetic.
close_reason: calmar_ratio now returns NaN when max_drawdown_pct is zero with positive CAGR, completing the quantwave-s3iu convention across the bundle. Denominator sweep also moved sharpe_ratio from 0.0 to NaN for zero dispersion with a non-zero mean; var_95/cvar_95 (quantiles, no denominator) and benchmark (None when undefined) were checked and left alone. Walk-forward grid selection extracted as select_best_objective and unit-tested for NaN-safety, TPE pool selector too. Docs: output-contract.md, changelog.md, skill docs. 1123 Rust tests pass, 14 python output-contract tests pass. Commit 6d0032df5.

title: MaStream silently substitutes SMA for every matype except EMA — APO, PPO, MACDEXT affected
description:
Found while scoping quantwave-wxii. Another silent-wrongness case: wrong number, no error.

quantwave-core/src/indicators/incremental/ma_stream.rs, MaStream::new:

    match ma_type {
        MaType::Ema => Self::Ema(TalibEma::new(period)),
        _           => Self::Sma(TalibSma::new(period)),   // <-- everything else
    }

The catch-all silently maps Wma, Dema, Tema, Trima, Kama, Mama and T3 to SMA. Callers get a plausible number computed with an algorithm they did not ask for, and nothing raises or warns. The enum only carries Sma and Ema variants, so the information is discarded at construction.

Consumers confirmed: APO and PPO (apo.rs, fast_ma/slow_ma) and MACDEXT (macd_ext.rs). So APO::new(12, 26, MaType::Wma) returns an SMA-based APO. STOCH also takes slowk_matype/slowd_matype and should be audited for the same path.

This is very likely not caught by the parity proptests because those construct with MaType::Sma — the same reason the BBANDS non-SMA fallback (quantwave-3nyh) went unnoticed.

All nine TA-Lib MaType variants ALREADY have native quantwave implementations: sma, ema, wma, dema, tema, trima, kama, mama, t3. So the fix is to route MaStream to those rather than collapsing to SMA. There is no missing-implementation excuse.

Fix: extend the MaStream enum to cover all nine variants, wiring each to its existing native streaming implementation. Add parity proptests parameterised over EVERY matype, not just Sma — that coverage gap is the root cause of this class of bug. If any variant genuinely cannot be supported incrementally, it must return an explicit error rather than silently substituting.

Related: quantwave-3nyh (BBANDS non-SMA fallback), quantwave-wxii (native MaType enum needed to drop the talib-rs runtime dep).
close_reason: Fixed and shipped. MaStream now dispatches all nine MaType variants to their native streaming implementations instead of collapsing seven of them to SMA. Verified on main 3b667bfdd through the Python surface: APO returns 9 DISTINCT values across the 9 matypes (previously Wma/Dema/Tema/Trima/Kama/Mama/T3 all silently returned the SMA result). Three new native impls were needed: TalibWma, TalibTema, TalibMama. STOCH audited for the same path. Parity proptests are now parameterised over every matype, not just Sma - that coverage gap was the root cause of this whole bug class and is now closed.

title: Document indicator conventions: stddev ddof=0, roc x100 vs rocp, atr non-Wilder vs ta_atr
description: Dogfood findings 1, 2, 3 -- these are TA-Lib conventions colliding with pandas defaults, not bugs, but each is a silent numeric footgun that needs prominent docs. (1) stddev is population std ddof=0 while pandas .std() defaults to ddof=1; differ by sqrt(N/(N-1)). (2) roc(N) returns x100 (TA-Lib); use rocp(N) for the plain price/price_N - 1 ratio -- silent 100x error otherwise. (3) atr(h,l,c,N) uses a non-Wilder smoothing matching neither pandas-Wilder nor SMA-ATR, while ta_atr matches TA-Lib exactly (Wilder RMA, SMA-seeded); document which to use, or consider defaulting atr to Wilder. Both roc/rocp and atr/ta_atr are registered and confirmed present.
notes:
CORRECTION (verified 2026-08-02): finding (3) in this issue is backwards. The Polars plugin pl.col('close').ta.atr('high','low',14) IS Wilder and matches TA-Lib exactly (= hand-computed 1.384819). The 3.496143 figure attributed to ta_atr came from calling it in the wrong argument order -- ta_* plugins need (high, low, close) with high in the receiver. See quantwave-sww3 (P0).

Findings (1) stddev ddof=0 and (2) roc x100 vs rocp are CONFIRMED correct as written:
  stddev = 1.9653244 (population) vs pandas .std() 2.0716338 (ddof=1)
  roc(10) = -0.830565 vs rocp(10) = -0.008306, exactly 100x
The real atr issue for docs is that the LIST API qw.ta.atr(14,h,l,c) = 2.903291 (EMA alpha=2/(period+1)) disagrees with the plugin of the same name -- see quantwave-xnaf.

# Epic: AI SEO (AEO/GEO) + Python/Rust AI-Enablement

Make QuantWave the authoritative, LLM-citable source for Polars-native quant TA, indicators, streaming parity, and backtest — across MkDocs, PyPI, and crates.io.

## Decisions (locked)

- **llms.txt**: hand-written v1 at `docs/llms.txt`, copied to site root on deploy
- **FAQ**: single `docs/faq.md` (not split Python/Rust)
- **Rust docs**: mirror **key** pages on MkDocs (crate map, Next<T>, streaming, backtest Rust path) + link to docs.rs for full API — do NOT duplicate full rustdoc
- **Indicator docs**: 217 guide pages remain canonical; mkdocstrings covers Python package surface only

## Architecture

```
MkDocs (lavs9.github.io/quantwave) = single narrative source of truth
  ├── llms.txt (AI crawler curator)
  ├── faq.md (extractable Q→A)
  ├── comparison.md, getting-started funnel (existing)
  ├── api/ (mkdocstrings — Python package)
  └── guides/rust/ (NEW — mirrored key Rust concepts)

docs.rs = Rust API depth (linked, not duplicated)
PyPI README + pyproject = discovery metadata aligned with docs
```

## Phase 0 — Fact consistency (P0)

- Unify **217** indicator count across README, pyproject, quantwave-python README
- Add `documentation` URLs to workspace + published Cargo crates (docs.rs)
- CI lint: fail on README/pyproject count drift vs metadata export

**Acceptance:** grep `150+` absent from user-facing metadata; `documentation` set on quantwave-core et al.

## Phase 1 — llms.txt + MkDocs AEO quick wins (P0)

- Add `!!! tip "Short answer"` to hubs: getting-started, comparison, backtest index, plugin_vs_ta
- Optional `docs/about.md` — ownership, citation preference, MIT

**Acceptance:** FAQ in nav; hub pages have answer-first admonitions

## Phase 3 — Python package top-class (P1)

- mkdocstrings: `show_signature_annotations`, `separate_signature`, selective `show_source`
- Docstring pass: `backtest`, `bt_polars`, `cli`, public `__init__` exports
- Optional `examples/*.py` referenced from README

**Acceptance:** `/api/` shows signatures; README examples match smoke test

## Phase 4 — Rust mirror on MkDocs + docs.rs (P1)

**MkDocs mirrored pages (curated, not full rustdoc):**
- `docs/guides/rust/index.md` — when to use Rust vs Python
- `docs/guides/rust/crate-map.md` — quantwave-core / polars / plugins / backtest → docs.rs links

- Expand `getting-started/rust.md` with links to mirrored guides + docs.rs badges

**Rust source quality:**
- Crate-level `//!` on quantwave-core, quantwave-backtest, quantwave-polars
- `///` + `# Examples` on Next, SuperTrend, BacktestEngine public API
- `examples/` for `cargo run --example`

## Phase 5 — Automation & governance (P2)

- Wire into `quantwave_verify.sh`
- Future: optional `gen_llms_txt.py` (not in v1 — hand-written only)

- Zero 150+ vs 217 drift in public files
- FAQ + comparison cited in AI spot-checks
- Copilot/Cursor correct `.ta` + `.bt` from in-repo docs

## Out of scope

- `navigation.expand` on full catalog

- llms-full.txt (P3 backlog)

title: Dependabot PR #38 CI failure is stale: rand 0.8/0.9 API mismatch against a main that has since changed
description:
Run 30391887027 on branch dependabot/cargo/rust-dependencies-aa7b5b2a20 (PR #38, still open) failed 2026-07-28 with 7+9 compile errors in quantwave-backtest.

Root error: E0599 no method named random_range found for StdRng / ThreadRng, at quantwave-backtest/src/tpe.rs:87 and elsewhere. The E0689 "cannot call sqrt on ambiguous numeric type" at tpe.rs:87 is a cascade -- u1 has no inferred type once random_range fails to resolve, so it is not a second independent bug.

random_range is the rand 0.9 name; gen_range is 0.8. Current main uses gen_range (tpe.rs:85-86 verified locally) and pins rand = "0.8" in the workspace Cargo.toml, though Cargo.lock resolves BOTH rand 0.8.6 and 0.9.4 via different dependents.

The PR branch is 5 days old and its CI ran against a main that has since moved (main is now at 081d6f9f6). The failure is therefore most likely staleness rather than a live defect on main -- main CI run 30378280619 passed. CONFIRM by rebasing PR #38 (or closing and letting dependabot reopen) and re-running, before spending time on a code fix.

If it still fails after a rebase, the real work is a rand 0.8 -> 0.9 migration: gen_range -> random_range, gen -> random, thread_rng -> rng, and the SeedableRng/from_entropy changes. Note there is precedent for deferring breaking dep bumps here -- see commit b0f1eb856 ignoring polars major/minor.
notes: Opened fresh PR #39 (https://github.com/lavs9/quantwave/pull/39) containing Dependabot's rand 0.9->0.10 bump squashed with the RngExt import fix (quantwave-backtest/src/tpe.rs and lib.rs test module) into a single atomic commit, per the constraint that neither ordering compiles alone. Verified locally before pushing: cargo build --workspace (0 errors), cargo nextest run --workspace (1138 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed). Closed PR #38 as superseded with an explanatory comment linking #39. Did NOT push onto Dependabot's branch (per user constraint) and did NOT merge #39 -- leaving this issue open until #39 actually merges.
close_reason: PR #39 merged 2026-08-12T04:01Z. rand 0.10 + RngExt fix landed on main as a single atomic commit. Dependabot PR #38 closed as superseded. Note during delivery: the first push of the branch silently reverted two NaN-safety regression tests in tpe.rs (test_tpe_select_from_pool_never_selects_a_nan_objective, test_tpe_select_from_pool_all_nan_falls_back_to_neg_infinity) because it was based on a stale WIP branch cut before those tests landed; caught before merge, restored, and the merged commit carries the full test set (workspace 1140 passed).

# Backtest Engine v0.2 Enhancement Epic – Design & QF-Lib Study (May 2026)

**Parent**: quantwave-n1yc (this epic)  
**Discovered-from**: quantwave-gwx (closed MVP), quantwave-b7u, quantwave-366  
**Status**: Research complete → ready for implementation tasks

## Executive Summary
The current `quantwave-backtest` crate (vectorized Polars long-format + hybrid `Next<T>` streaming parity) is already a strong foundation and correctly chose the high-performance path over pure event-driven models.

This epic captures the **targeted, high-leverage enhancements** needed to reach institutional/research quality on par with (or better than) the best ideas from:
- **QF-Lib** (Apache 2.0) – particularly its mature `InitialRiskPositionSizer` driven by rich `Signal.fraction_at_risk` metadata, clean `CommissionModel` + `Slippage` trait design with sophisticated realistic models, and professional tearsheet/reporting output.
- **vectorbt** / best polars-backtest patterns – for analytics depth, speed, and rich output.

**Core constraint (non-negotiable)**: All enhancements must preserve 100% backward compatibility with the existing vectorized batch + streaming parity guarantees. No switch to event-driven core.

## 1. QF-Lib Study – Position Sizing with Rich Metadata (Most Valuable)

### Key Artifact: `Signal` class + `InitialRiskPositionSizer`

From QF-Lib source (`qf_lib/backtesting/signals/signal.py` + `initial_risk_position_sizer.py`):

```python
class Signal:
    ticker, suggested_exposure, fraction_at_risk, last_available_price,
    confidence, expected_move, alpha_model, ...
```

**InitialRiskPositionSizer** (the money shot):

```python
target_percentage = self._initial_risk / signal.fraction_at_risk
target_percentage *= signal.suggested_exposure.value   # direction
target_percentage = self._cap_max_target_percentage(target_percentage)
```

Then it feeds `target_percent_orders(...)`.

**Direct applicability to QuantWave PA work**:
- A `FlagPattern` or `HsPattern` (from quantwave-r46a / bfg) can expose `fraction_at_risk` (or `recommended_risk_pct = k / pole_height_atr`, or `1.0 / strength`).
- The position sizer becomes "sized by pole height" or "sized by pattern conviction" with almost zero glue code.
- Same pattern works for any future geometric or regime-based rich struct.

**Current state in quantwave-backtest**:
- We already have `size_multiplier_col` and streaming `StrategySignal` with metadata (good).
- But no dedicated `RichMetadataPositionSizer` trait + default impl that understands `fraction_at_risk` / `risk_budget` semantics the way QF-Lib does.
- No `max_leverage_cap` or per-signal risk budgeting yet.

**Proposed enhancement**: New `RichRiskPositionSizer` (or trait) that can consume either simple f64 exposure or rich structs containing `fraction_at_risk` / `risk_contribution`.

## 2. QF-Lib Study – Execution Model Design (CostModel + Slippage)

### Clean Abstractions (highly recommended to port/adapt)

**CommissionModel** (abstract):
```python
class CommissionModel(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def calculate_commission(self, fill_quantity: float, fill_price: float) -> float: ...
```

Concrete impls: `BpsTradeValueCommissionModel`, `FixedCommissionModel`, `IBCommissionModel`.

**Slippage** (more sophisticated base):
- `process_orders(date, orders, no_slippage_prices) -> (fill_prices, fill_volumes)`
- Built-in support for `max_volume_share_limit` (critical for realistic large orders).
- `SquareRootMarketImpactSlippage`:
  ```python
  market_impact = price_impact * volatility * sqrt(fill_volume / ADV)
  fill_price = no_slippage_price * (1 + sign * market_impact)
  ```
  Uses recent volatility + ADV (very good model).

Other models: `PriceBasedSlippage`, `FixedSlippage`.

**Current QuantWave state** (`CostModel` in lib.rs):
```rust
pub struct CostModel {
    commission_bps: f64,
    slippage_bps: f64,
    initial_cash: f64,
}
```
Very basic constant-bps model. No volume awareness, no market impact, no pluggable trait, no per-asset configuration.

**Proposed enhancement**:
- Define `CommissionModel` and `SlippageModel` traits in Rust (with good defaults).
- Implement at minimum: Bps, Fixed, and a SquareRootMarketImpact variant (with volatility + ADV estimation helpers).
- Add `max_volume_share_limit` support in the high-fidelity path.
- Make the "High-Fidelity Execution Simulator" mode use the rich models while the fast vectorized path can still use the simple bps version for speed.

This directly enables the "high-fidelity execution simulator mode" mentioned in the original recommendation.

## 3. QF-Lib Study – Reporting Output Shape & Quality

QF-Lib excels at producing institutional-grade artifacts after every backtest:
- Full Tearsheet (performance stats, drawdowns, risk metrics)
- Transactions log (very detailed)
- Trades Analysis Sheet (win rate, avg duration, best/worst trades, by direction, by holding period, etc.)
- Portfolio Analysis (concentration, turnover, exposure over time)
- Timeseries exports
- PDF + Excel + interactive charts

The key is that the reporting layer receives rich trade + signal objects and can attribute performance back to specific alpha models / PA patterns / features.

**Current QuantWave state**: Basic `Trade` struct + equity curve + some stats. Not yet at tearsheet quality.

**Proposed enhancement**: 
- Rich `BacktestResult` / `Tearsheet` types that can serialize to Polars + high-quality Markdown/PDF/Excel (or Python-side rendering using the existing Python bindings).
- Explicit support for attaching PA pattern metadata (e.g. "this trade was triggered by Flag #42 with pole_height=3.2 ATR, score=87") to trades for later attribution analysis.

## 4. High-Fidelity Execution Simulator Mode (the big idea)

**Vision** (preserving current architecture):
- The existing vectorized batch path (`run_batch`) and streaming parity path continue to use the fast/simple `CostModel` (or a lightweight version) for maximum speed during research sweeps.
- Add a new `run_high_fidelity_simulation(...)` (or configurable mode) that:
  - Takes the **exact same** vectorized signals / `StrategySignal` stream (including rich metadata).
  - Replays them through a much more realistic `ExecutionSimulator` that uses the full QF-Lib-inspired `CommissionModel` + `SlippageModel` stack (square-root impact, volume limits, partial fills, etc.).
  - Still produces identical trade list / equity semantics for parity testing (just with more realistic costs).
- This gives the best of both worlds: lightning-fast research + believable live-like P&L when you are ready to promote a strategy.

This is the concrete realization of the recommendation made after the initial QF-Lib study.

## Sources Recorded
- All QF-Lib files studied (May 2026):
  - `qf_lib/backtesting/signals/signal.py`
  - `qf_lib/backtesting/position_sizer/{position_sizer.py, initial_risk_position_sizer.py, ...}`
  - `qf_lib/backtesting/execution_handler/{commission_models/*.py, slippage/*.py, simulated_execution_handler.py, ...}`
  - `qf_lib/backtesting/execution_handler/slippage/base.py`
- GitHub: https://github.com/quarkfin/qf-lib (Apache-2.0)
- Docs: https://qf-lib.readthedocs.io/
- Current QuantWave code: `quantwave-backtest/src/lib.rs` (as of 2026-05)
- Related bd: quantwave-gwx (closed), quantwave-06sz (rich Struct integration), quantwave-ug9t (parity)

## Next Steps (Child Tasks)
See the linked child tasks created under this epic. They are deliberately vertical slices so they can be claimed and delivered incrementally without breaking existing parity tests.

This epic closes the loop on the "make the backtester as good as the best open tools while staying true to QuantWave's unique strengths (Polars speed + Next<T> parity + rich PA/ML structs)" objective.
notes: All subs closed (1 sizer impl+wired+tested, 2/3 models+HighFid impl+wired, 5 integration+tests, 06sz rich PA verified/enhanced, 4 tearsheet scoped). Code in worktree (cargo check + tests pass), merged in landing. Backtest v0.2 now has rich metadata sizer (pole/fraction from PA), pluggable realistic execution models, HighFid mode, config support, parity preserved. Closes the epic.

design:
# Detailed Design: quantwave-n1yc.1 — Rich-Metadata-Aware Position Sizer

**Epic**: quantwave-n1yc (Backtest Engine v0.2)  
**Priority**: 1  
**Depends on**: None (foundational for high-fidelity sizing)  
**Enables**: quantwave-n1yc.3 (High-Fidelity mode), quantwave-n1yc.5

## Problem Statement
The current backtester has basic support for sizing via:
- Simple f64 signal columns
- `size_multiplier_col` (ad-hoc)
- Streaming `StrategySignal` with metadata (good start in ug9t/06sz)

However, there is **no first-class, reusable abstraction** for "rich risk-aware position sizing" that directly consumes the kind of metadata our PA detectors (Flags from Part 69, H&S from Part 66, Market Structure, etc.) will naturally emit:
- `fraction_at_risk` / `recommended_risk_pct`
- `pole_height_atr`
- `strength` / `score`
- `conviction`

QF-Lib solves this elegantly with `Signal.fraction_at_risk` + `InitialRiskPositionSizer`:
```python
target_pct = initial_risk / signal.fraction_at_risk * direction
```

We need the Rust/Polars equivalent that feels native and works for both batch (Polars expressions) and streaming (`Next<T>`) paths.

## Goals
- Provide a clean `RichPositionSizer` trait + at least one powerful default implementation (`InitialRiskPositionSizer`).
- Make it trivial for PA detectors to influence sizing via rich metadata (e.g. "size this Flag breakout to risk 1.5% of portfolio based on its pole height").
- Support caps (`max_target_percentage`, `max_leverage`).
- Work seamlessly with the existing `StrategySignal` / rich Struct system.
- Preserve (and improve) batch vs streaming parity.

## Non-Goals (for v0.2)
- Full portfolio optimization / covariance-based allocation (future epic).
- Live broker integration (this is still simulation).

## Proposed Design

### Core Trait
```rust
// In quantwave-backtest/src/position_sizing/mod.rs

pub trait PositionSizer {
    /// For batch/vectorized path: given a LazyFrame with rich signals + OHLCV,
    /// produce a column of target exposures (f64, can be >1 or negative).
    fn size_batch(
        &self,
        lf: LazyFrame,
        config: &PositionSizingConfig,
    ) -> PolarsResult<LazyFrame>;

    /// For streaming path: given a StrategySignal (which may contain rich metadata),
    /// current portfolio state, and latest bar, compute the desired target exposure.
    fn size_streaming(
        &self,
        signal: &StrategySignal,
        portfolio: &PortfolioState,
        current_bar: &Bar,
    ) -> f64;   // target exposure (e.g. 0.75 = 75% of portfolio)
}
```

### Key Supporting Types
```rust
pub struct PositionSizingConfig {
    pub initial_risk: f64,                    // e.g. 0.02 = risk 2% per trade
    pub max_target_percentage: Option<f64>,   // hard cap on leverage
    pub tolerance_percentage: f64,            // for target_percent logic
    // Future: per-symbol overrides, etc.
}

/// Rich signal that PA detectors will emit (already partially exists)
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct StrategySignal {
    pub exposure: f64,                    // -1.0 .. +1.0 or 0
    pub metadata: Option<SignalMetadata>, // the rich part
    // ...
}

pub struct SignalMetadata {
    pub fraction_at_risk: Option<f64>,    // from PA detector
    pub pole_height_atr: Option<f64>,
    pub strength: Option<f64>,
    pub pattern_id: Option<u32>,
    pub regime_prob: Option<f64>,
    // ... extensible via HashMap or enum for now
}
```

### Default Implementation: `InitialRiskPositionSizer`
```rust
pub struct InitialRiskPositionSizer {
    pub initial_risk: f64,
    pub max_target_percentage: Option<f64>,
}

impl PositionSizer for InitialRiskPositionSizer {
    fn size_batch(...) { ... }   // Polars expr: initial_risk / fraction_at_risk * exposure
    fn size_streaming(...) { ... }
}
```

**Batch implementation sketch** (very efficient):
```rust
let target = (initial_risk / col("fraction_at_risk"))
    .clip(0.0, max_target)
    * col("exposure");
```

This is exactly what QF-Lib does, but vectorized.

### Integration Points
- Batch path: User can call `.ta.backtest.with_position_sizer(...)` or manually apply the sizer before feeding to engine.
- Streaming path: The `run_streaming_simulation` already accepts `Next<... Output=StrategySignal>`. The sizer becomes a small wrapper or is applied inside the simulation loop when building orders.
- Existing `size_multiplier_col` remains as a simple fallback / escape hatch.

### Parity Requirements
- For any given set of rich signals, the batch `size_batch` and streaming `size_streaming` must produce **bit-identical** target exposures (within floating point tolerance) when fed the same data.
- This must be covered by proptests in the parity harness (task .5).

## Sources
- QF-Lib (May 2026 study):
  - `qf_lib/backtesting/signals/signal.py`
  - `qf_lib/backtesting/position_sizer/initial_risk_position_sizer.py`
  - `qf_lib/backtesting/position_sizer/position_sizer.py`
- Current QuantWave: `quantwave-backtest/src/lib.rs` (StrategySignal, size_multiplier_col, 06sz work)
- PA detectors: quantwave-r46a (Flags), previous bfg H&S work

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New `position_sizing` module with trait + `InitialRiskPositionSizer`
- [ ] Works with both simple f64 exposure and rich `StrategySignal` containing `fraction_at_risk`
- [ ] `max_target_percentage` cap implemented and tested
- [ ] Batch and streaming paths produce equivalent results (proptest)
- [ ] Example in docs / canonical notebook using a real PA struct (e.g. Flag with pole_height)
- [ ] Full documentation + source citations in code
- [ ] cargo nextest + clippy clean

## Risks / Open Questions
- How to handle cases where `fraction_at_risk` is missing or zero in rich structs? (Proposal: fall back to 1.0 or configurable default, with warning.)
- Should the sizer also influence stop-loss placement? (Out of scope for this task, but noted for future.)

This task is the highest-leverage single improvement for making PA detector outputs actually actionable in the backtester.

# Detailed Design: quantwave-n1yc.2 — Pluggable CommissionModel + SlippageModel

**Epic**: quantwave-n1yc  
**Priority**: 1  
**Enables**: quantwave-n1yc.3 (High-Fidelity mode)

## Problem Statement
Current `CostModel` is too simplistic:
```rust
pub struct CostModel {
    commission_bps: f64,
    slippage_bps: f64,
    ...
}
```
It only supports constant basis-point costs. It has no concept of:
- Per-asset or per-order realistic models
- Volume limits
- Market impact that scales with order size and volatility
- Pluggable behavior for "fast research" vs "high-fidelity validation"

QF-Lib has a much more mature design with abstract `CommissionModel` and `Slippage` traits, plus several high-quality implementations (including `SquareRootMarketImpactSlippage` with ADV and volatility).

## Goals
- Introduce clean, extensible traits:
  - `CommissionModel`
  - `SlippageModel`
- Implement at least 4 realistic models (inspired directly by QF-Lib + common industry practice).
- Support `max_volume_share_limit` as a first-class citizen.
- Make it easy to swap "fast" vs "high-fidelity" models at runtime/config.
- Keep the hot path (simple bps) extremely cheap when high fidelity is not needed.

## Proposed Traits

```rust
pub trait CommissionModel: Send + Sync + Debug {
    fn calculate_commission(
        &self,
        fill_quantity: f64,
        fill_price: f64,
        symbol: Option<&str>,
    ) -> f64;
}

pub trait SlippageModel: Send + Sync + Debug {
    /// Returns (adjusted_fill_prices, actual_fill_volumes)
    fn apply_slippage(
        &self,
        date: DateTime<Utc>,
        orders: &[Order],
        no_slippage_prices: &[f64],
        market_volumes: Option<&[f64]>,   // for volume-aware models
    ) -> (Vec<f64>, Vec<f64>);
}
```

## Planned Implementations (v0.2)

1. **BpsCommissionModel** (current behavior, very fast)
2. **FixedPerShareCommissionModel**
3. **BpsTradeValueCommissionModel** (QF-Lib style)
4. **SquareRootMarketImpactSlippage** (highest value)
   - Uses recent volatility + ADV
   - Formula: `impact = price_impact * vol * sqrt( |qty| / ADV )`
   - Includes `max_volume_share_limit` enforcement
5. **PriceBasedSlippage** + **FixedSlippage** (for completeness)

Also provide a `CompositeExecutionModel` that combines one Commission + one Slippage.

## Configuration
```rust
pub enum ExecutionModelConfig {
    SimpleBps { commission_bps: f64, slippage_bps: f64 },
    HighFidelity {
        commission: Box<dyn CommissionModel>,
        slippage: Box<dyn SlippageModel>,
    },
}
```

The engine can select the mode per run or per symbol.

## Parity & Performance
- The simple bps path must remain allocation-free and very fast (used in research sweeps).
- High-fidelity path can be slower (used when validating a candidate strategy).
- For any given set of orders + prices, the high-fidelity path must be deterministic and reproducible.

## Sources
- QF-Lib (May 2026):
  - `execution_handler/commission_models/commission_model.py`
  - `execution_handler/commission_models/bps_trade_value_commission_model.py`
  - `execution_handler/slippage/base.py`
  - `execution_handler/slippage/square_root_market_impact_slippage.py`
- Current code: `quantwave-backtest/src/lib.rs` (CostModel)

## Acceptance Criteria
- Traits defined + at least 3 concrete impls (Bps, Fixed, SquareRootMarketImpact)
- `max_volume_share_limit` fully supported in slippage models
- Easy configuration switch between "fast" and "high-fidelity" modes
- Unit + property tests for each model
- Documentation with formulas and examples
- No regression in existing fast-path performance (benchmark)

## Risks
- Estimating ADV and volatility inside the simulator for the square-root model (we may need a small rolling statistics helper or accept it as input).

This task is a prerequisite for any credible "high-fidelity" mode.

Matches design in epic. n1yc.2 closed.

# Detailed Design: quantwave-n1yc.3 — High-Fidelity Execution Simulator Mode

**Epic**: quantwave-n1yc  
**Priority**: 1  
**Depends on**: n1yc.1 (Rich Sizer) + n1yc.2 (Models)

## Problem Statement
Today we have one execution path (with simple costs). Researchers either accept unrealistic costs for speed, or they slow everything down.

We want the **best of both worlds**:
- Blazing fast vectorized + streaming paths for research and parameter sweeps (using lightweight costs).
- A believable, high-fidelity "pre-live" validation path that applies sophisticated realistic execution (market impact, volume limits, better commissions) **while still being driven by the exact same rich signal stream**.

This is the concrete realization of the recommendation after studying QF-Lib.

## Core Idea
Add a new method (or mode) on the backtest engine:

```rust
impl BacktestEngine {
    /// Fast research path (existing behavior, enhanced with new simple models)
    pub fn run_batch(&self, config: &BacktestConfig, signals: LazyFrame) -> BacktestResult { ... }

    /// High-fidelity path - same signals, much more realistic execution
    pub fn run_high_fidelity(
        &self,
        config: &BacktestConfig,           // will contain ExecutionModelConfig::HighFidelity
        signals: impl IntoStrategySignals, // can be batch DF or streaming generator
    ) -> BacktestResult { ... }
}
```

Key property: For the **same input signals** (including rich `StrategySignal` metadata), the high-fidelity mode must produce the same *trade decisions* (entry/exit timing and direction) — only the realized prices and costs differ.

## Architecture
- Reuse the existing order generation logic (now powered by the new Rich Position Sizer from task .1).
- Introduce an `ExecutionSimulator` trait/abstraction that the engine can swap.
  - `FastExecutionSimulator` (current simple bps logic)
  - `HighFidelityExecutionSimulator` (uses full `CommissionModel` + `SlippageModel` stack from task .2, plus potential future partial-fill logic)
- The high-fidelity simulator still operates on the vectorized/ streaming signal stream — it does **not** require switching to an event-driven engine.

## Data Flow (High-Fidelity)
1. User provides same rich signals / `Next<T>` generator as before.
2. Position sizing happens (can use rich metadata).
3. Instead of simple bps, orders are passed to `HighFidelityExecutionSimulator`.
4. Simulator applies realistic slippage (possibly volume-limited, market impact) and commission.
5. Fills are recorded with much richer `Fill` metadata (slippage_reason, market_impact_component, volume_share_used, etc.).
6. Same downstream analytics + reporting pipeline.

## Parity Requirements
- Trade *timing and direction* must be identical between fast and high-fidelity paths when using equivalent sizing logic (this is the important parity).
- Cost and fill price differences are expected and desired.
- We should still be able to run the full batch-vs-streaming parity tests even when high-fidelity mode is selected.

## Sources & Inspiration
- QF-Lib `SimulatedExecutionHandler` + realistic slippage models (May 2026 study)
- Industry practice for "research vs production" backtest modes (common at quant funds)

## Acceptance Criteria
- New `run_high_fidelity` (or equivalent) exists and is documented
- Can be driven by both batch rich DataFrame and streaming `Next<T>` generators
- Uses the new pluggable models from task .2
- Produces richer `Fill` / `Trade` records that capture the extra realism
- Parity tests (task .5) cover "same decisions, different costs" scenario
- Example in the canonical notebook shows the difference between fast and high-fidelity P&L on the same PA+ML strategy

This is the flagship feature of the v0.2 epic.

# Detailed Design: quantwave-n1yc.4 — Professional Tearsheet & Reporting Layer

**Epic**: quantwave-n1yc  
**Priority**: 2

## Problem Statement
Current output is functional (equity curve, basic Trade list, some stats) but not at the level serious quants or PMs expect when deciding whether to allocate capital.

QF-Lib shines here: after every backtest you get a rich, attributable PDF/Excel tearsheet package that includes:
- Performance summary + risk metrics
- Detailed transaction log
- Trade analysis (by direction, duration, size, PA pattern, etc.)
- Portfolio exposure & concentration over time
- Signal attribution (which alpha model / PA detector drove the P&L)

We need something of comparable quality while staying native to Polars + rich Struct world.

## Goals
- Define a rich, serializable `BacktestTearsheet` / `BacktestReport` data model.
- Provide at least one high-quality output renderer (Polars → Markdown + Excel is minimum; PDF optional via Python bindings).
- Make it trivial to attach PA / feature / regime metadata to trades for later slicing and attribution.
- Support both batch and streaming runs.

## Proposed Output Structure

```rust
pub struct BacktestTearsheet {
    pub summary: PerformanceSummary,           // CAGR, Sharpe, Sortino, Calmar, max DD, etc.
    pub risk_metrics: RiskMetrics,             // CVaR, Omega, etc.
    pub trades: Vec<EnrichedTrade>,            // Trade + attached PA metadata
    pub fills: Vec<EnrichedFill>,
    pub equity_curve: DataFrame,               // Polars DF
    pub exposure_over_time: DataFrame,
    pub attribution: AttributionReport,        // by symbol, by PA pattern type, by regime, by feature bucket
    pub config_snapshot: BacktestConfig,
}
```

`EnrichedTrade` should be able to carry arbitrary metadata from the originating `StrategySignal` (e.g. `pole_height_atr`, `flag_score`, `regime_at_entry`).

## Rendering
- Core: Produce the `BacktestTearsheet` struct + Polars DataFrames.
- Convenience: `report.to_excel(path)` and `report.to_markdown()` (using polars + Rust crates or delegating to Python quantwave side).
- Future: PDF via WeasyPrint-style pipeline (inspired by QF-Lib) if demand exists.

## Integration
- The engine (both batch and high-fidelity) should return a rich `BacktestResult` that contains or can produce the tearsheet.
- Rich PA signals already flowing through the system (from 06sz) should automatically be captured in the attribution section.

## Sources
- QF-Lib document generation and tearsheet modules (May 2026 study)
- Common institutional backtest report standards
- Current `Trade` struct in quantwave-backtest

## Acceptance Criteria
- `BacktestTearsheet` (or equivalent) struct defined with good serialization
- At least one renderer that produces a professional-looking Excel + Markdown report
- Automatic capture of rich signal metadata into trades and attribution
- Example output checked into the repo / docs for the canonical strategy
- Works for both fast and high-fidelity runs

This task turns the backtester from "useful research tool" into "decision support system".

# Detailed Design: quantwave-n1yc.5 — Integration, Parity Tests & Canonical Example

**Epic**: quantwave-n1yc  
**Priority**: 1  
**Depends on**: All previous children (1-4)

## Purpose
This is the "make it real" task. It proves that the v0.2 enhancements work together, deliver value on top of real PA + ML signals, and do not break any of the hard-won parity guarantees from the gwx MVP era.

## Scope

### 1. Cross-Feature Integration
- Wire the new `RichMetadataPositionSizer` (task 1) into both batch and streaming paths.
- Make the engine support `ExecutionModelConfig::HighFidelity` (tasks 2+3) end-to-end.
- Ensure the new rich reporting (task 4) receives and displays PA metadata (pole height, pattern score, etc.).

### 2. Parity & Correctness Testing (Critical)
Must add / extend proptests that cover:
- Same rich signals → same trade decisions in fast vs high-fidelity mode (only costs differ).
- Batch `size_batch` + high-fidelity execution produces equivalent results to streaming `size_streaming` + high-fidelity execution (within documented tolerance).
- Rich PA structs (Flag, H&S, etc.) flowing through the entire stack without data loss or look-ahead.

Use the existing parity harness pattern from `quantwave-ug9t`.

### 3. Canonical Example Update
Update (or create a new version of) the flagship notebook:

**"Flag breakout sized by pole height, filtered by Ehlers features + regime, with high-fidelity execution and full attribution"**

This notebook must:
- Use real (or high-quality synthetic) PA detector output from the cu03 work.
- Demonstrate the new rich position sizer.
- Show side-by-side fast vs high-fidelity P&L and trade lists.
- Produce and display the new professional tearsheet output.
- Be part of docs CI / examples.

### 4. Documentation & Migration
- Update crate-level docs explaining the two execution modes and when to use each.
- Add a "v0.2 Migration / New Features" guide.
- Record all new sources (QF-Lib study + this epic).

## Acceptance Criteria
- All new v0.2 features exercised together in one canonical end-to-end example using rich PA signals.
- Expanded parity test suite passes (including high-fidelity variants).
- No regressions in existing fast-path tests.
- Professional tearsheet output is generated and looks good for the canonical strategy.
- Full source citations and design decisions recorded in code + bd.
- `cargo nextest` + `clippy -- -D warnings` clean on the backtest crate.

## Success Signal
A quant can take a strategy built with the new PA detectors + ML features, run it in high-fidelity mode with realistic execution, and get an institutional-quality report that clearly shows the contribution of specific patterns and features — all while the fast research path remains fast and parity is maintained.

This task is what turns the individual improvements into a coherent, trustworthy v0.2 release of the backtester.

title: Introspection registry: fill 23 None-valued param defaults + fix beta/correl input_names
description:
Live verification of p2k0.1 (the df.ta.all() unlock) found the discovery layer solid (221 fns, groups, output shapes all correct) but the parameter-schema layer has a bounded completeness gap that would make a generic caller (df.ta.all / screeners) crash or produce wrong results:

1. 23 functions report a None-valued param default via abstract.Function(name).parameters — e.g. alma.offset/sigma=None, ichimoku.tenkan/kijun/senkou_b=None, donchian.period=None, frama.period=None, hurst_exponent.period=None. Passing **parameters sends offset=None -> crash. Root: defaults derive from inspect.signature() on the .ta PyO3 method; where that param has no signature default, it falls to None with no authoritative fallback.

2. beta and correl declare input_names=['close'] but are TWO-series functions (beta of two series; correlation of two series). A generic caller feeds one series -> wrong/failing.

NOT in scope / not a defect: ~98 indicators are streaming-only (no batch .ta path) and correctly raise NotImplementedError; df.ta.all() must skip those by design.

Also NOT the fix: naively switching the defaults source to the curated _metadata registry — verified that registry itself diverges from the callables for some indicators (bbands _metadata uses std_dev/period=20 while the real .ta.bbands uses timeperiod=5; abstract correctly reports 5). The introspection must stay aligned with the actual callable; fix the missing values at their true source (the .ta plugin / Rust constructor defaults), not by swapping registries.

Acceptance: every batch-capable function's abstract.parameters has no None default; beta/correl/other 2-series fns declare correct input_names; a positive-control test asserts no None defaults across the batch-capable set; this unblocks p2k0.2 (df.ta.all()).

title: [WINS-MAJOR] New capabilities — ranked feature roadmap from the July 2026 competitive scan
description:
Source: planning/BRUTAL_REVIEW_2026-07-07.md + competitive landscape scan (July 2026).
Context: QuantWave's moat is being the only MIT-licensed, Polars-native, full-breadth TA +
backtest stack (Yvictor's polars-backtest is PolyForm Noncommercial; vectorbt is
Commons-Clause). Direct new threat: Wickra (github.com/wickra-lib/wickra, launched May 2026,
514 indicators, O(1)/tick streaming, WASM + 7 language bindings) is claiming QuantWave's exact
"Rust-core streaming parity" positioning. These ten features are ordered by leverage. D1→D2→D6
form a dependency chain (introspection registry → bulk compute → ML features).
PREREQUISITE: the UGLY epic (credibility fixes) should land before marketing any of these.

title: Indicator introspection registry — TA-Lib Abstract-API equivalent (get_functions / get_function_groups)
description:
PROBLEM / OPPORTUNITY
TA-Lib's decades-long adoption moat is not its math — it's the abstract API: get_functions(),
get_function_groups(), and per-function metadata (input names, parameters with defaults, output
names) that let screeners, no-code UIs, optimizers, and migration tools integrate ALL functions
generically without hardcoding signatures. polars_talib users expect exactly this. QuantWave has
the raw data (per-indicator IndicatorMetadata consts incl. LaTeX formula + citation;
metadata_export.json with 221 entries) but NO public runtime API exposing it. This single
feature is what turns "another TA library" into "a TA-Lib replacement targets can migrate to."
design:
RUST: public registry module in quantwave-core exposing an iterator over all IndicatorMetadata:
name, group/category, input schema (which OHLCV columns / series), parameters (name, type,
default, valid range), output schema (names, types, struct fields for multi-output), warmup
length, talib_name where an equivalent exists (see BAD epic B7), citation.
PYTHON:
- quantwave.get_functions() -> list[str]
- quantwave.get_function_groups() -> dict[str, list[str]]
- quantwave.abstract.Function(name) façade mirroring talib.abstract semantics: .input_names,
  .parameters (dict with defaults), .output_names, __call__(df_or_arrays, **params) dispatching
  to the real implementation.
SINGLE SOURCE: this registry must be THE source feeding docs catalog generation, the canonical
indicator count (UGLY U3), .pyi stub codegen (BAD B3), and _TALIB_MAP (BAD B7). One metadata
system, many consumers.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD
1. Rust: registry iterator count == number of compiled indicators; property test: every entry
   has non-empty inputs/outputs; every param default lies within its declared valid range.
2. Python: union of get_function_groups() values == get_functions(); no duplicates.
3. Parity contract: for 5 sampled indicators (incl. one multi-output, e.g. MACD), calling via
   abstract.Function(name)(df, **defaults) equals the direct .ta call result exactly.
4. Docs drift: the native catalog page regenerates from the registry with zero diff.
ACCEPTANCE
- talib.abstract-style usage documented in the migration guide; a generic "screener" example
  notebook iterates all functions via the registry.
close_reason: Merged in PR #13 (squash). TA-Lib abstract-API introspection registry: qw.get_functions(), qw.get_function_groups() (union==functions, no dupes), qw.abstract.Function(name) with .input_names/.parameters(defaults)/.output_names/.info and __call__ (named dict/DataFrame or positional arrays) dispatching to parity-tested .ta plugins (multi-output->tuples). Rust registry_introspection.rs property tests (4). Docs guides/talib_migration.md + screener example. All 4 acceptance criteria met. CI green.

title: Live execution bridge — India brokers (paper-first) per the deferred Nautilus ADR
description:
PROBLEM / OPPORTUNITY
planning/NAUTILUS_LIVE_BRIDGE_ADR.md exists but is explicitly deferred. The Options India
analytics stack (unique differentiator) currently ends at analysis — no execution path. Indian
users specifically want NSE broker hooks (Zerodha Kite / Upstox / Fyers). vectorbt PRO and
RaptorBT increasingly blur backtest→live. BIGGEST LIFT on this list — sequence LAST, after the
credibility (UGLY) and testing (BAD) epics are done.
design:
PHASE 1 (this issue):
- Stable signal-export contract: schema for streaming signal events (aligns with the rich-Struct
  PA output philosophy), consumable by any executor.
- ONE reference broker adapter (Upstox official SDK or Kite Connect) behind `quantwave[live]`
  extra. PAPER-TRADING MODE IS THE DEFAULT; live orders require explicit arming (config +
  runtime flag).
- Hard safety requirements: dry-run default, explicit order-arming, client-side rate limiting,
  idempotent order keys (duplicate signal → single order), global kill switch.
PHASE 2 (separate future issue): Nautilus Trader adapter per the ADR.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD
1. Contract tests against broker sandbox/mocked recorded fixtures: auth, place, modify, cancel,
   reject, partial-fill paths.
2. Paper-mode simulation: recorded signal stream → expected order-intent fixture (golden).
3. Idempotency: replaying the same signal twice produces exactly one order intent.
4. Kill-switch test: armed session + kill → zero further order intents.
5. NO live-money tests in CI, ever. Sandbox/mock only — state this in the test README.
ACCEPTANCE
- Paper-trade tutorial in docs; ADR updated to reflect phase-1 implemented; safety checklist
  documented.
notes: Deferred out of p2k0 (2026-07-19): epic-sized on its own (live money + broker OAuth/order state machines, external SDK, sandbox-only testing). Revisit as its own epic later. LiveBridge trait + RecordingLiveBridge stub already exist in quantwave-backtest/src/live_bridge.rs per planning/NAUTILUS_LIVE_BRIDGE_ADR.md.

title: Bulk compute API — df.ta.all() (pandas-ta strategy("all") equivalent)
description:
PROBLEM / OPPORTUNITY
pandas-ta's killer ergonomic is df.ta.strategy("all"): compute the entire library onto a frame
in one call — the standard move for exploration and ML feature matrices, and the reason
pandas-ta-classic holds 388 stars despite pandas performance. QuantWave requires hand-writing
221 expressions; this is its biggest ergonomic gap. With the D1 registry, closing it is
mechanical — and Polars lazy evaluation makes it FASTER than pandas-ta by construction.
design:
API: df.ta.all(include=None, exclude=None, groups=None, params={name: {...}}) plus
qw.feature_matrix(df, ...) alias returning (df, feature_column_names).
MECHANICS (built on D1 registry):
- Resolve each indicator's required input columns from registry input schema; skip indicators
  whose inputs are absent from the frame (recorded, not raised).
- Execute as a single lazy with_columns batch so Polars parallelizes.
- Multi-output indicators expand struct fields to prefixed columns (e.g. macd_signal).
- Returns the frame plus a manifest: computed list, skipped list with reasons, per-indicator
  timing (optional flag).
- Column-name collision policy: registry-prefixed, deterministic.
- Generated .pyi (BAD B3) covers the new API.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD
1. On a sample OHLCV frame: all() computes >= (registry count minus documented exclusions)
   columns, no exceptions; warmup NaN policy consistent with per-indicator metadata.
2. Equality: each produced column equals the individually-computed indicator (randomly sample
   20 per CI run; full sweep nightly).
3. include/exclude/groups filters honored exactly (set algebra tests).
4. Missing-column handling: frame without `volume` skips the volume group with manifest reasons;
   nothing raises.
5. Perf smoke: 100k rows, full all() completes under a recorded threshold (informational
   benchmark harness entry).
ACCEPTANCE
- One-liner featured in README quickstart; example notebook (exploration -> feature matrix);
  docs page with the manifest contract.
close_reason: Merged PR #19. df.ta.all()/feature_matrix (121 computed/100 skipped), quantwave.mtf (lookahead-safe), quantwave.datasets (synthetic+load_sample). 231 python tests, sanity+wheel-smoke green. Follow-ups: adx output_names, geometric_patterns perf.

title: Multi-timeframe (MTF) helpers — lookahead-safe resample, apply, and broadcast
description:
PROBLEM / OPPORTUNITY
Zero resample/timeframe code exists anywhere in the repo, yet "compute on the higher timeframe,
act on the lower one" (daily HMM regime → 5-min bars) is in EVERY practitioner workflow and is
a top forum request across pandas-ta/vectorbt communities. Users currently hand-roll
group_by_dynamic + join_asof — and routinely introduce lookahead bias doing it. A lookahead-safe
helper is cheap to build and directly showcases the regime suite (unique strength).
design:
Module quantwave.mtf (Python/Polars-level first; Rust later only if profiling demands):
- ohlcv_resample(df, every="1d", by="symbol"): canonical OHLCV aggregation
  (first/max/min/last/sum) via group_by_dynamic, tz-aware.
- mtf_apply(df, every, exprs, by=...): resample then compute arbitrary .ta expressions on the
  higher timeframe.
- mtf_broadcast(base_df, higher_df, on="ts", by=..., suffix=...): join higher-TF results back
  to base-TF rows via join_asof with STRICTLY-PAST semantics — by default the higher-TF value
  broadcast at time t is from the last COMPLETED higher-TF bar (i.e. shift(1) on the higher
  frame). Lookahead-safe by construction; an explicit allow_current_bar=True override exists
  for the rare intentional case.
- Multi-symbol aware throughout (by= grouping).
acceptance_criteria:
TDD — lookahead is THE risk; write these first:
1. Anti-lookahead property test: construct synthetic data where the in-progress higher-TF bar
   differs wildly from the completed one; assert the broadcast value at every base-TF time t
   equals the last COMPLETED higher bar strictly before t (never the in-progress bar).
2. Resample parity: ohlcv_resample vs a hand-written group_by_dynamic gold fixture.
3. Timezone / session boundaries: tz-aware fixtures in IST and UTC; DST-transition fixture;
   assert bucket edges are correct.
4. Multi-symbol isolation: symbol A's values never leak into symbol B (property test with
   disjoint value ranges).
5. Incremental consistency: computing on the full frame equals computing on an
   incrementally-grown frame (aligns with the batch/streaming parity philosophy).
ACCEPTANCE
- Docs guide "Multi-timeframe analysis" featuring daily-regime→intraday example; used in at
  least one example notebook.
close_reason: Merged PR #19. df.ta.all()/feature_matrix (121 computed/100 skipped), quantwave.mtf (lookahead-safe), quantwave.datasets (synthetic+load_sample). 231 python tests, sanity+wheel-smoke green. Follow-ups: adx output_names, geometric_patterns perf.

title: Data layer — bundled sample dataset, synthetic generator, and fetch/cache connectors (incl. NSE)
description:
PROBLEM / OPPORTUNITY
The getting-started funnel requires the user's own Parquet file; no sample data, no shown
output, no connectors — the #1 first-ten-minutes friction (site review). vectorbt PRO treats
built-in data access as core. And for the Options India stack (QuantWave's unique
differentiator) there are no NSE data loaders at all.
design:
a. quantwave.datasets.load_sample(): bundle a small (~1-2MB) license-clean sample —
   NIFTY index + 2 liquid stocks, daily ~10y + 5-min ~3mo. VERIFY licensing for redistribution;
   if exchange data can't be redistributed, ship a realistic calibrated synthetic instead and
   say so.
b. quantwave.datasets.synthetic(seed, ...): deterministic OHLCV generator (GBM + regime switches
   + volume model) — shared with the benchmark harness (UGLY U2) and docs examples.
c. quantwave.data fetchers (optional extra `quantwave[data]`, keeping core install lean):
   - yfinance thin wrapper -> Polars frame with canonical schema.
   - NSE: bhavcopy (EOD) downloader, option-chain snapshot loader — document NSE ToS
     constraints explicitly; polite rate limits; no scraping beyond published endpoints.
   - Local parquet cache directory with freshness policy.
d. Canonical schema contract (column names, dtypes, tz) documented — all loaders emit it, all
   examples assume it.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD
1. load_sample(): offline test (bundled file, zero network) validating the schema contract
   (columns, dtypes, tz-awareness, monotonic ts).
2. synthetic(): determinism test — same seed → identical frame hash; regime-switch statistical
   sanity (variance differs across regimes).
3. Fetchers: network-mocked tests with recorded responses; cache-hit test proves second call
   makes zero network requests; corrupted-cache recovery test.
4. End-to-end: the docs quickstart snippet (using load_sample) executes in CI (snippet-runner)
   — this is the "10-minute path" proof.
ACCEPTANCE
- Quickstart works with zero external data; NSE loaders documented with ToS note; [data] extra
  installable separately.
close_reason: Merged PR #19. df.ta.all()/feature_matrix (121 computed/100 skipped), quantwave.mtf (lookahead-safe), quantwave.datasets (synthetic+load_sample). 231 python tests, sanity+wheel-smoke green. Follow-ups: adx output_names, geometric_patterns perf.

title: Portfolio optimization engine (mean-variance, risk parity, HRP)
description:
PROBLEM / OPPORTUNITY
QuantWave's own capability matrix lists portfolio optimization as "not implemented"; the
shared-capital portfolio sim exists but there is no weight optimization. vectorbt PRO and every
serious backtesting stack treat this as table stakes. Completes the portfolio story the
backtester already half-tells, and pairs with the regime suite (regime-conditional allocation)
for a differentiated angle.
design:
Home: a portfolio module in quantwave-backtest (or sibling crate if it grows).
- Covariance estimators: sample, EWMA, Ledoit-Wolf shrinkage.
- Optimizers: min-variance & max-Sharpe (quadratic via nalgebra; closed-form where possible),
  risk parity (Spinu fixed-point iteration), HRP (López de Prado hierarchical clustering —
  correlation-distance linkage + recursive bisection).
- Constraints: long-only, per-asset weight bounds, full-investment budget.
- Polars API: returns frame in, weights frame out; rebalance-schedule integration with the
  existing backtest engine (weights → target positions → orders) and walk-forward compatibility.
- Regime hook (differentiator): optional regime-label column → per-regime covariance/weights.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD
1. Gold fixtures: fixed return matrices → weights vs PyPortfolioOpt/riskfolio-lib reference
   outputs (store fixtures with generator script + versions).
2. Properties: risk-parity risk contributions equal within tol; HRP weights sum to 1 and
   respect bounds; min-variance portfolio variance <= equal-weight variance on the same cov.
3. Ledoit-Wolf vs sklearn.covariance.LedoitWolf gold fixture.
4. Integration: backtest with periodic re-optimization reproduces a deterministic equity-curve
   fixture (seeded synthetic data).
5. Degenerate inputs: singular covariance, single asset, NaN returns → typed errors (no panics
   — follows the de-panic standard from the BAD epic).
ACCEPTANCE
- Docs Backtest section gains a Portfolio Optimization page; capability matrix updated;
  regime-conditional allocation example notebook.
close_reason: Merged PR #21. quantwave.portfolio (min_var/max_sharpe/risk_parity/hrp, Ledoit-Wolf, typed errors; Python-first, Rust port deferred) + quantstats interop (backtest_returns/to_quantstats). 329 tests, no-deps smoke verified.

title: ML feature namespace — functime-class bulk extraction with a regime/DSP edge
description:
PROBLEM / OPPORTUNITY
functime (1.2k stars) proves demand for bulk panel-data feature extraction on Polars. QuantWave
holds inputs nobody else has (HMM regime probabilities, Ehlers DSP cycle/trend decompositions,
rich multi-output indicators) but offers no bulk feature surface — docs/ml_features.md is a
guide without a product behind it. Prior internal research (beads quantwave-4ps/tha/wlx/gw7s)
already scoped this.
design:
API: qw.features.extract(df, feature_sets=["ta_core","ehlers","regimes","rolling_stats"],
by="symbol", horizon=...) built on D2's bulk compute:
- Leakage-safe by construction: every feature at time t uses information <= t only.
- Label helpers: forward returns over horizons; triple-barrier labels (López de Prado
  definition: profit-take/stop-loss/time barriers).
- Split helpers: purged K-fold / walk-forward time splits with embargo.
- Output contract: (features_df, feature_names: list[str], metadata incl. per-feature warmup).
acceptance_criteria:
TDD — leakage first:
1. Leakage property test (FIRST test written): mutate all rows strictly after time t with
   extreme values → features at t must be bit-identical. Run over every feature set.
2. Purged/embargo split tests: zero index overlap between train and test after purge+embargo
   (property test over random parameters).
3. Triple-barrier gold fixtures: hand-constructed price paths with known first-touch outcomes.
4. Batch/streaming parity: features from batch extract == accumulated streaming computation for
   indicators supporting Next<T> (reuses existing parity infra).
5. Integration smoke: features → LightGBM/sklearn fit on sample data without NaN errors after
   warmup trim.
ACCEPTANCE
- End-to-end notebook in docs: extract → train → evaluate → feed signals into the existing
  backtest engine.
close_reason: Merged PR #20 (main). qw.features.extract (leakage-safe, 4 sets, 192 feats verified 0-leak), forward_returns/triple_barrier (gold-fixture), purged_kfold/walk_forward. End-to-end + no-deps wheel smoke verified. 296 python tests.

title: QuantStats-compatible tear-sheet interop
description:
PROBLEM / OPPORTUNITY
QuantWave has native HTML tear sheets, but the ecosystem standard for performance reporting is
QuantStats (vectorbt PRO integrates it directly). Users comparing engines want their familiar
reports; forcing a proprietary tear sheet creates switching friction. Interop is cheap: emit
returns in the shape QuantStats expects.
design:
1. BacktestResult gains .returns(freq=...) → tz-aware series (pandas Series for QuantStats
   compatibility; polars native also available) with documented resampling rules for intraday.
2. .to_quantstats() convenience behind an optional extra (quantstats not a hard dep).
3. Document the metrics mapping (our Sharpe/MDD definitions vs QuantStats') and any known
   tolerance differences. Keep the native tear sheet as default.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD
1. Golden cross-validation: a known equity-curve fixture → returns series consumed by
   quantstats.reports.metrics() without error, AND QuantStats' Sharpe/MaxDrawdown match the
   engine's own metrics within documented tolerance (this cross-validates BOTH metric
   implementations — the real value of the issue).
2. Frequency/tz edge tests: daily vs intraday resample; IST-tz backtest exported correctly.
ACCEPTANCE
- Docs page "Using QuantStats with QuantWave"; tolerance table documented.
close_reason: Merged PR #21. quantwave.portfolio (min_var/max_sharpe/risk_parity/hrp, Ledoit-Wolf, typed errors; Python-first, Rust port deferred) + quantstats interop (backtest_returns/to_quantstats). 329 tests, no-deps smoke verified.

title: WASM target + in-browser indicator playground in the docs
description:
PROBLEM / OPPORTUNITY
Wickra already ships WASM bindings (plus Node/.NET/Go/Java/R) — in-browser computation is
becoming table stakes for Rust-core TA libraries, and a live docs playground is the single best
marketing asset a docs site can have. QuantWave's streaming Next<T> API is a natural WASM fit
(no Polars dependency needed for the streaming path).
design:
1. New quantwave-wasm crate (wasm-bindgen): expose a curated streaming-indicator subset
   (RSI, EMA, SuperTrend, MACD, CyberCycle, Ichimoku...) via the Next<T> path; feature-gate any
   polars/std-heavy deps out of the wasm build of quantwave-core if needed.
2. Build npm package (wasm-pack); CI job builds the wasm target on every PR touching core
   (prevents bit-rot).
3. Docs playground page: lightweight-charts (or similar) + live indicator computation over the
   bundled sample/synthetic data, parameter sliders. Fully self-contained static assets.
acceptance_criteria:
TDD
1. wasm-pack test (node): streaming RSI/EMA/SuperTrend outputs vs the Rust gold fixtures —
   bit-identical f64 (extends the parity guarantee to a third runtime; strong marketing claim).
2. Size budget test: gzipped wasm bundle under a set threshold (e.g. 1.5MB) — fails the build
   if exceeded.
3. CI wasm build job green on PRs.
4. Optional playwright smoke: playground page loads, computes, renders.
ACCEPTANCE
- npm package built in CI (publish decision separate); playground live on the docs site.
notes:
Split into MVP-first + full engineering (2026-07-21):
  • quantwave-stb8 (P2, READY) — WASM marketing MVP: curated live playground, visibility-first, ship ASAP.
  • quantwave-hwxa (P3, blocked by stb8) — full engineering: npm package, CI wasm job, size budget, node parity, full coverage. Kept for the future.
The original DESIGN/ACCEPTANCE below now lives in hwxa; do the MVP first for reach.

title: Alternative bar types (Renko / Kagi / Point&Figure / range bars) + harmonic patterns
description:
PROBLEM / OPPORTUNITY
Wickra lists market profile and Renko/Kagi/P&F bar families; these plus harmonic patterns
(Gartley/Bat/Butterfly) are perennial retail requests that TA-Lib never served. QuantWave
already has the foundations: geometric_patterns.rs / pattern.rs, swing/pivot infrastructure,
and the internal MQL5 PA research (ATR-adaptive measurable rules, rich Struct signal outputs
separate from visualization — see beads memories on the MQL5 PA Toolkit series).
design:
1. Bar-construction transformers (ohlcv/tick → alternative bars): Renko bricks (fixed + ATR box),

title: Stale test_sma_parity encodes wrong .ta mental model (LazyFrame.ta, qw.PySMA)
description:
PROBLEM
tests/python/test_parity.py::test_sma_parity has been failing and is dead legacy predating 5ipk.2 (which superseded it with 25 gold-vector parity tests). It fails on TWO stale API assumptions:

1. line 13: df.lazy().ta.sma('close', period) -> AttributeError: 'LazyFrame' object has no attribute 'ta'.
   The .ta namespace is registered via @pl.api.register_expr_namespace('ta') in _ta_namespace.py, i.e. on pl.Expr, NOT on LazyFrame/DataFrame.
   Correct form: pl.col('close').ta.sma(3)
2. line 28: qw.PySMA(period) -> does not exist. The real streaming class is qw.streaming_class('sma') -> Sma.

NOT a math problem: the expected values [1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, ...] are CORRECT and match live 0.7 output exactly. Only the two API calls are stale.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A RED TEST
This test teaches the exact misconception that derailed a full investigation of quantwave-84cu: an agent probing the 0.7 surface concluded df.ta was 'not auto-registered' and built a false narrative (that 0.7 had moved SuperTrend to the .ta expression namespace) on top of it, nearly triggering an unnecessary downstream compiler refactor. A failing test in-repo asserting LazyFrame.ta is an authoritative-looking source for a wrong mental model.

DECISION NEEDED
(a) Repair (~2 lines): pl.col('close').ta.sma(3) + qw.streaming_class('sma'). Keeps an explicit, readable .ta-expr-vs-streaming parity demo that documents the correct surface.
(b) Delete as superseded: gold_parity already covers SMA numerically.
Recommend (a) — the demo value is precisely the misconception it currently causes.

ACCEPTANCE
- tests/python/ has 0 failures from this file
- test uses the Expr namespace and a real streaming class
- if kept, add a one-line comment noting .ta binds to Expr, not LazyFrame/DataFrame

CONTEXT
Found while fixing quantwave-84cu (PR #14, dc2ea89a4). Confirmed pre-existing via git stash on a clean tree; not caused by that change.
close_reason: Merged in PR #15 (1ede17ffe). Repaired to pl.col().ta.sma() + streaming_class('sma'); math was already correct.

title: stddev one-pass precision loss on low-variance inputs; use Welford/two-pass
description: Dogfood finding 4. stddev loses ~1e-6 relative precision on low-variance inputs due to a one-pass algorithm and catastrophic cancellation. Immaterial to results but trips a strict 1e-7 parity gate. Consider a two-pass or Welford accumulator for numerical stability.
